item.title: Welcome Home, Dayz Roox
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
But, when we purchased the car, I had been interested in something a bit smaller than what I had at the time, and I wasn't keen that it was white. ... than my last car, the price was right (it was cheap), and my car at the time was really starting to look old (though it performed wonderfully; it was a Mazda Premacy).
...But, in the end, we purchased it (it was a good deal) and we have so far received great service from the staff.
Upon pickup today, we received final instructions on the car's use, finished the last of the paperwork, and were even given a bottle of non-alcoholic wine as a present!! A further bonus is that this car company is a 5 minute drive from our house, so should there be questions or need of service, it is close at hand.

item.title: New Textbooks
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
There often seem to be a lot of odd jobs for me to do once I have 'free time' from my university lessons.
One of those tasks in recent years has been working on the textbooks I sell through Amazon.com. ... Things mostly went OK this spring, but there were a few hiccups to deal with, and thankfully (I hope) they have all been dealt with.
...I don't know if there have been changes at Amazon, but the final product this year seems to be a higher quality than before, even though I found the quality in the past was very good.
...In a few short weeks, classes will begin again, and both students and I will be using the textbooks in our lessons.

item.title: Christmas Cookies
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
One of the things I like best about Christmas is the baking. I love the planning, making, baking, and eating.
...Every year we try to let the younger students at our school enjoy decorating their own Christmas cookies.
Those students who study with us for several years become experts at this activity.
Even more fun for the students, they get two

item.title: O-Live-U (I love you)
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
One of the lucky finds in Japan for me has been that olives are grown here, and that most people do nothing with them.
...But, every once in a while, they are good for snacking. Sometimes they are used in cooking.
...They don't require much work to pickle them, and they last for a long time.
One more item from my list of fall tasks has been checked off.

item.title: Swinging in the Wind
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It had been about 17 years from when we built our house, and it certain places, the paint needed to be another coat.
...One of the things I did was to remove various hooks and objects that I'd attached to the house siding over the years before the painters came.
...When we first built our house and put up our signs, I did so quickly and with the intention of changing the setup as was needed. However, with time, I found that things worked okay, and so I never did any changes to the setup.
...Luckily, I found things that could be used, and with a couple more items, I was ready to go.

item.title: Stollen
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I saw a post on social media late last year in which someone made Stollen and it looked so good that I kept the idea in my head. ... Usually I buy a mixture of dried fruits and spices from a baking shop, and the mixture is more than enough for one fruitcake (which is what I make).
...I've never made it before, so after looking at a few recipes, I decided to follow the recipe at Simply Recipes, as I always have good results from the recipes at that site.
...It's similar to my traditional fruit cake, but it's also spiced a bit differently, it's lighter, it has crunchy bits and soft bits, and it's difficult to stop at one piece.
I will be making this recipe again in the future and urge others to try it if you haven't yet.

item.title: My Textbook is a Best Seller
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
After the spring semester of university classes finished, I allowed myself a bit of a break, but soon had to get to work on things for the fall. This involved writing 2 new textbooks, formatting them, getting them uploaded, working on design, and then, finally waiting.
I'm really pleased that one of my textbooks, for now at least, is best seller on Amazon Japan. I know it will not last, and I know I will not be rich or famous because of my work, but I am pleased none the less.
...I think it is important to enjoy the little rays of sunshine that sometime cross our path in life.

item.title: My First Covid-19 Vaccination
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I have been waiting for a Covid-19 vaccination for a long time.
I've been following the science on the vaccination story, and have seen how effective it has been around the world.
...I know that I'm only partly protected now, but it's a start.
...I will have to wait and see how my body reacts after the second dose of the vaccine, due to be received next month.
...The journey is not over, for there Is still much ground to be covered.

item.title: Jaws, Covid-19 & the Olympics
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
A testament of the skill of this movie is that even though there were a number of scenes my 12-year old self did not watch, the movie was tremendously enjoyable, scary, and entertaining.
...The movie doesn't hold the same impact on me now, but the world has changed, and my knowledge of things has increased.
...This led to me think about the situation with Covid-19, and more recently the Olympics that are to be held shortly here in Japan, in July 2021. Just like in the movie Jaws, while some individuals are worried about the health of citizens, others in power focus mostly on the economy.
...In the run-up to the Olympics here in Japan, do athletes want to compete, do individuals want to come see and cheer, does the world want to take part in an international event?

item.title: Ukrainian Food
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
While the beets grew, they had leaves which we picked and enjoyed many, many times.
...I was able to make one medium pot of borscht soup, using what vegetables we had on hand. ... Traditionally my family would add some sour cream to the soup, but sour cream seems very expensive here in Japan, so I opted for a bit of cream.
A few weeks ago we'd had a feast of perogies, and luckily we were able to freeze some for another day.
Along with the borscht and perogies, we had some dill pickles on the table, and some pickled beets.

item.title: My New Textbooks
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I guess that many people who teach try to take a bit of a break between school terms.
...In years past, I have used textbooks in my classes that I made and printed myself.
...2020's pandemic threw a wrench in that tradition so I had to try new things. While I had looked at publishing my books elsewhere in the past, it always seemed a lot of work and trouble. ... In the second half of that year, I succeeded with both an ebook and printed book.

item.title: Beet Leaf Buns
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I'm not sure why, but the taste of those buns made some deep connection within me, such that after some time, here in Japan, I desired those buns.
...Then, pieces of the dough are wrapped in beet leaves, covered with dill, green onions, salt and pepper and cream, then left to rise again.
...Often, I make these and serve with homemade tomato soup (another recipe from my mother).
...Each time I make them, my skill improves, and I move closer to my mother's standard.
...But, tomorrow is a day that has beet leaf buns in it.

item.title: To my university students, many thanks.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Now that I have finished all the lessons, testing, and grading, it is time to reflect.
...With online lessons using the internet, some things work better than in-person lessons, some worse, some just as well.
...To those students I taught, thank you for your participation and help during the year. At the end of my classes I had some comments from some students and I appreciated all of it.
If students enjoyed my lessons and wish to continue practicing English with me, please contact me at my school.

item.title: おお掃除 / Big Cleaning
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
My memory tells me that in Canada, a major cleaning for one's house took place in the Spring, when one could hang things outside again to dry or air, when one could open the windows for fresh air, and when it was time to clean up from the Winter.
...The idea is one that is a big similar in some other cultures though, namely to get rid of the dirt from this year, so that the new year can start clean.
...I'm a bit sad to see the Christmas decorations and objects put away for another year, meaning that this time is over.
...Much time was spent cutting, fitting and glueing a new piece over the cracked area, instead of just taping it and moving on.
...Now we just have to wait for Spring, when once again we open the windows, put things out for airing, and do much, much cleaning.

item.title: My Boxing Day
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Being Canadian, Boxing Day brings up memories of sales after Christmas, sometimes incredibly low-priced items being offered for sale.
I have memories of my one and only Boxing Day shopping adventure when I went to buy a CD player (back in the 90's) that was listed very cheap, but in limited supply.
With others I did not know, I stood outside the store before 6 AM in bitterly cold weather waiting for the store to open, hoping that it was not a waste of my time.
...When the doors opened, I along with others rushed inside (politely, no pushing) towards the back of the store where an employee was standing by a large stack of new, boxed CD players, literally throwing them in front of him as shoppers like myself grabbed one and moved aside.
...Japan does not have Boxing Day, but very similarly has items for sale on January 1st (sometimes before, and sometimes even after) of mystery lucky bags (福袋).

item.title: Year-end Treats
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
At the end of the school year at Canada Club English School, we like to give something to our students, especially since this is the season of giving.
...But this year, 2020, we felt that the idea of sharing foods with others might not be the best idea.
...We decided that a year calendar would be an appropriate gift to students. It took some work to get the design right, to add all the Japanese holidays, to choose a picture, and to get it printed and laminated.
...2020 has been an interesting year, but we now look forward to 2021.

item.title: Fondue
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We use wine, kirsch, and cheese, cooked in a bowl rubbed with garlic. Into the fondue, we use bread, of course, and if people want, we also add sausages, cooked potatoes, and cooked broccoli. We buy a pre-shredded cheese, and don't worry about being truly authentic.
...The cheese and the bread are the main stars, and they never fail to shine.
Winter is just beginning, and there's a fair chance we'll enjoy fondue once more this winter.

item.title: カナダクラブのコロナ対策
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
生徒間、生徒と講師間にアクリル衝立版を設置しています。
...教室にダイキンの空気清浄機を設置。 各レッスンごとの換気に加えて、空気清浄機で常時空気を綺麗にしています。
...各レッスンごとに講師が机、椅子、ドアノブ、アクリル衝立版を塩素系漂白剤で消毒しています。
...全員マスク着用を徹底し、手指の消毒をしています。

item.title: New Safety Measures
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The latest changes we've made to our school, to better protect both staff and students are shown in the two photos above.
Barriers for each student in class will help to provide more protection for everyone, while allowing students to interact with other members and also provide ample room for students to work with printed materials during class.
A new air cleaner will provide cleaner air within the classroom to further protect all members.
We care about the safety of everyone involved in our English classes and want to try to continue to provide face-to-face lessons, with all the various interactions that normally take place among members and the teacher.
Please come and enjoy our English classes.

item.title: Yes, I Put Basil in the Ratatouille.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The first time I made ratatouille long, long ago was after picking fresh vegetables from a farm in Canada.
I was awestruck by the simplicity of the recipe, but the depth of flavour. ... With really fresh produce, not much is needed to produce something delicious.
...Not as good as the first time, but what can ever match the first time?
...Not many ingredients are needed, and not much work is needed.

item.title: 焼き鳥/やきとり/yakitori/grilled chicken
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It's almost summer.
...Teriyaki.
Skewers.
Yakitori. /やきとり。

item.title: Baby Lemons
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Well, we don't have any lemons ready for making lemonade, but we do have lemons growing in our garden.
We've not had any citrus growing in our garden before, but last year when we went to a nursery looking for new plants, we talked with the staff.
...The lemon tree was one of the plants we bought, and it has survived the winter and it began to bloom this spring. It's nice to see that some of the blooms have given way to tiny little lemons growing on the tree.
Now we will have to wait and see how many of these tiny lemons grow into full-sized lemons.

item.title: Thai Grilled Pork Skewers - Moo Ping
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Japan has yakitori (焼鳥), the delicious grilled skewers of chicken which are so delicious to eat.
...Recently I came across a recipe for Thai skewers of pork that sounded interesting.
Af first, I was looking at the recipe from Milk Street, but eventually I used the recipe at Serious Eats because they were more generous with sharing information. You can find the recipe here: https://www.seriouseats.com/recipes/2019/07/thai-style-grilled-pork-skewers-moo-ping.html
...We made a cucumber salad with Thai flavors, and also a peanut sauce (just because we had made peanut butter earlier in the day and wanted to use some of it).

item.title: A Big Mess
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Over the last 2 months, we've had to adjust, like so many others in the world, due to the virus that is affecting lives everywhere.
We shut our school for many lessons in March, and then in April made the decision to stop in person lessons.
Quickly we've had to adjust our lessons to the reality of the times, using the internet to teach online lessons. After teaching for over 20 years, a teacher has many tools to teach in many different situations. ... We've had to develop a new toolbox with lesson ideas and techniques, to teach students from age 4, up to adult lessons.

item.title: Chewy Dulce de Leche Squares
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
If you've never heard of dulce de leche before, or ever seen it, this is not a problem.
As far as I understand it, dulce de leche is the result of cooking sweetened condensed milk until it is golden and caramel-like. Often this can be done by taking a can of condensed milk, putting it in a pot, covering the can with water, and gently cooking it for 30-45 minutes, then carefully opening the can.
...For this recipe, I needed more than one can's worth of dulce de leche, because the cans I can buy are a little small.
...Unfortunately, it didn't have enough caramel flavor for me, so I quickly made a small amount of caramel, added it into the dulce de leche, and my mixture was ready.

item.title: Weekly Shopping
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
My parents had roughly the same idea, go shopping once for the week rather than buying everyday, and buy a number or basic goods that can be used for all sorts of recipes.
...In our house, we roughly plan out the next week's menu before we go shopping. We try to stay within a budget, using the same amount of money each week.
...As an example, one of our purchases today was a package of cheese, 4 squares of 8 grams of cheese, which come in a variety of flavors. ... Later in the day, visiting another store just by chance, we checked what items they had.

item.title: Filo Dough
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I've been in this situation before, so I knew I could either order filo dough over the internet and wait one or two days to make it, or, I could make the filo dough myself.
...Filo dough is a simple dough recipe and it just requires practice and time to get the sheets of dough nice and thin. They will never be as thin as store-bought filo as long as I'm making it, but that's OK. They still taste great and the recipe will still turn out OK.
I made 9 sheets of filo dough in total and it was perfectly enough for my square baking dish.
...The spanakopita baked well, with a golden, crispy top, and the spinach mixture inside was yummy and creamy.

item.title: Food for Friends
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Not only do we enjoy their beautiful sounds, colours and activity, we also enjoy the ability of birds to help control the amount of insects in our garden.
I've tried various methods over the years to encourage more birds to visit, but our yard design, being enclosed on 3 sides, means birds are scared to enter the area.
Last year, I visited Canada and picked up a block of bird seeds wrapped in netting that could be used for bird feeding.
With winter upon us, it took me a while to find a place to hang this food.
Today, after some simple purchases at the ¥100 store, I was able to hang the food in front of our kitchen window, and provide a place for the birds to perch while eating the food.

item.title: Grilled Chicken Caesar Sandwich
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It's a long weekend and I received my daily email from Bon Appetit magazine, filled with various recipes.
...The recipe is called Grilled Chicken Sandwich with Caesarish Dressing, and the photo they posted looks much better than our final product.
...A marinade is divided in half at the beginning, half for the chicken to marinade, the other half becoming the mayo for the sandwich.
...When we put the burgers together and began eating, they tasted great and disappeared quickly.
...This recipe is definitely one that we will make again because it was easy to make, tasted great, and was satisfying without us feeling stuffed.

item.title: Osechi 2020/ 2020のお節料理
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We have just finished (burp!, excuse me) our traditional Japanese New Year's breakfast.
...Ozoni is soup made with miso or other ingredients, and includes mochi, plus maybe other vegetables or even meat.
...Our Osechi included many foods, but I'll explain what I had on my plate. From the bottom left and going clockwise, I had Onishime, which are various foods cooked in a broth, kuromame or black beans, marinated salmon, fried chicken, roast beef, and in the centre, kurikinton (sweet potatoes and chestnuts).
...This was/is a nice way to start the new year.

item.title: Here's to Longevity!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Toshikoshi soba (年越し蕎麦) are noodles that are traditionally eaten at the end of the year. One reason they are eaten is that the length of the noodles represents a long life.
...My family likes to have soba noodles, and to have some tempura to enjoy with the noodles and soup, like vegetables and shrimp.
...All of these noodles are long as well, so I guess they also can represent a long life.
As 2019 comes to a close, I wish everyone a Happy New Year, and longevity fo all!

item.title: Christmas Cookies 2019
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Christmas has many traditions, but one that I like to share with my younger students is the joy of making cookies.
...They decorate cookies and then at the end of the lesson, they take their cookies home to share with their family, or just enjoy by themselves.
...My mother made a variety of cookies and baked treats throughout the year, but at Christmas time there was much more to sample.
...By the end of elementary school, students are not only good at making cookies, but seem comfortable in the kitchen. Thus, the students not only learn about a cultural activity, but they also learn a life skill that in a small way will help them in their future.

item.title: 2019 Halloween Baking Party
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It's that time of the year when scary things happen, sweets are abundant, and people walk around in crazy costumes.
Our school's 2019 Halloween event was again a baking party.
...Some of the creations made by students included 2 types of cookies, jack-o-lantern cookies and witch hat cookies, 2 types of scary rice balls, and mummy sausages.
Laughs, cookies, sweets and trick-or-treating made for a fun party.
Many thanks to those who helped, and to those who came.

item.title: Indigo Dyeing (藍染め) at Studiio N2
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Terrible person that I am, I tend to get absorbed in what I am doing, what I am eating, who I am talking to or what I am watching. ... Unfortunately, this means that I am usually not an individual that is constantly snapping pictures in many social or personal situations. I had such a good time during my weekend outing, that little did I think of using a camera to take pictures.
...Detailed instructions were given, and many examples of dyeing were shown to us, so that we could decide how we would do our dyeing.
...The time seemed to pass in a flash and I can't thank the staff enough for such a great time.

item.title: 2019 Canadian Election
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
For a number of years under the former, conservative Prime Minister of Canada, the honorable Stephen Harper, I and many other ex-pats from Canada were not allowed to participate in the democratic act of voting for elected officials in Canada's national elections.
...Under the current Prime Minister of Canada, Justin Trudeau, individuals such as myself once more have the right to vote in national elections.
...There are some in Canada (and Canadians living abroad) who my gripe with issues at times, yet fail to participate in elections. ... Throughout history, we've seen cases of amazing things that occurred due to the actions of one person, yet time and time again, many individuals feel that they, as an individual can do good by participating in elections for the governing officials.
...I urge all that if you live somewhere that allows you the right to participate in an election, then please do so.

item.title: Fall is Upon Us
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We are still experiencing temperatures around 30 degrees Celsius and above, with high humidity and we are moving deeper in September.
...This is a sight observed this morning when out on my morning walk, and it, to me, conveys fall.
...Hanging the rice to dry is traditional though not seen as much nowadays as many farmers use electric dryers for their rice.
...The pattern of the sun has already been changing from its summer path.
...On and on, the changes will come, the season will change, and then before we know it, winter will be upon us.

item.title: Tests Finished
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
While I enjoy teaching my classes at the 2 universities I teach at part-time, the grading period is something l'm not crazy about.
...There was so much material to go through and I was sure it would take me over one week to pour over all the material, but hard work over 4 or 5 days allowed me to finish the job much sooner than anticipated. I checked and double-checked, and finally at the end of last week, I was finally able to submit the final grades for the first term at the 2 universities.
With that work done, I can now work on cleaning areas that were not cleaned very much over the past few weeks, including our parking lot (lots of weeds), and enjoying some of what summer has to offer.
I now have a couple of months to think, make notes, prepare, and be ready for the fall term of university classes that will begin in October.

item.title: Salsa - My Burning Fingers
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We've had lots of peppers this year in our garden, including green peppers, jalapeños, and another type of hot green pepper, the name of which is unknown to me. We've also had some tomatoes and other vegetables and herbs, but it's the peppers that are producing like mad and for which I was looking for new ideas.
...First I roasted most of the vegetables on my grill outdoors, which softened them, gave them a different smell and flavor and allowed for the pepper skins to be removed.
...The balance of flavors, the heat from different peppers created a salsa that tastes great on its own - not too spicy, but with a good kick of heat - but better with chips or other foods.
This was my first year to make salsa, but because of the great result, I will be making this again and again from now on.

item.title: The University of Manitoba
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It's been a long, bumpy ride getting here, but at long last we've arrived! One of my daughters will start attending the University of Manitoba from the fall, 2019.
...We wish her best of luck with her studies and her life at university.
...If anyone knows of a room for rent, or a small apartment for rent, we'd appreciate the help.
While the journey getting here has finished, this new journey will begin soon, and there is still much to do.

item.title: Pssst! Wanne See Something Dirty?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
If there is too much, the soot can eventually catch fire, and this could potentially be dangerous as chimney pipes are not designed to have a fire burning inside them.
...I use a plastic bag to collect the soot, but it's an imperfect procedure, as there is always soot that escapes the bag and winds up around me, and in the general vicinity of the wood stove.
...Before cleaning, I must removed one section of pipe, then physically move the wood stove away from the rest of the pipe, so that I can feed in the brush and the poles connected to the brush. ... To get the wood stove on to the slats, I must use my car tire jack to raise the wood stove, one side, then the other, to get the slats under the wood stove legs.
...After the area is cleaned up, the wood stove can be moved back into place, lowered off of the slats, and the piece of removed pipe once more connected to the rest of the pipe and stove.

item.title: Ume Jam
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Ume, or Japanese Apricot (梅) is often used at this time of year for making pickled plums, or umeboshi/梅干し . I've made them in the past, but in recent years I've been making ume jam.
Ume is very, very sour and tart and it requires a lot of sugar to balance the flavor. But the final result is a jam full of pectin that thickens beautifully, is sweet and tart, and is a beautiful orange yellow color.
We use ume jam on bread and pancakes, but it is also very good with meats that are grilled when used as a glaze.

item.title: 2019 Tacos Party
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We enjoyed our annual Tacos Party this weekend with our younger students.
Games were played, tortillas were made, and tacos were eaten.
We cooked, we ate, we talked, we laughed.
It was a great party. Looking forward to next year!

item.title: Buns for Easter - Don't be Cross
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
This year, I did a quick internet search for recipes, even though I have a recipe that I've used in the past successfully. ... It takes some time, so I had to pass on making it yesterday, leaving for today, Easter Sunday (for those who follow such holidays).
...I ended up having to add more flour, and when trying to shape the dough it was still quite sticky, so that the buns were not smooth.
...I didn't want to make a cross using flour and water (there's no taste in that), so I considered making the cross with the icing.
...I gave up the idea of making a cross, thinking that these buns needed to be free from any religious connotations and instead decided to slop on some of that delicious icing.

item.title: Spring Garden - Renewal
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Today, much to the dismay of the bees and other insects around here, we pulled out our kale, Swiss chard, sorrel, and arugula.
...We've been able to put away in the fridge some cooked Swiss chard stems, and Swiss chard leaves, washed and ready for salads or sandwiches.
...We'll add some more plants over the next couple of weeks and then let the gardens get to work with their own community.
Though our garden may be small, it serves us well and provides plenty of food over the year, as well as beautiful plants to look at, provide shelter, and smells, and contribute to our well-being. I'm always surprised so many new houses are built and families do NOT put in any space for a garden, however small.

item.title: White Day 2019
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Traditionally in Japan, mostly women gave chocolates to men on Valentine's Day, and men returned the favour by giving something sweet and or white on White Day.
...Somewhere I'd recently seen a picture of children making some giant baseball-sized cookies that were round and white, and this became my inspiration. ... Further searching led me to Snowball cookies, or Russian Tea Cakes (there seems to be a wide variety of names for the same cookie).
I found a variety of recipes and took some ideas from this one, and some from that one to hobble together a recipe.
...The sugar coating is sweet, but it is balanced by the pinch of salt I added (some recipes don't add it) and the nuttiness of the almonds (those crazy nuts).

item.title: I Think I Have It...
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
One night, in Vancouver, we had dinner at a Persian restaurant, and while everyone else had some kind of kebab or other meat dish, I went with a vegetarian entree, namely roasted eggplant.
...A recent cooking experience suggests that I've come pretty close to replicating, at least in my mind's eye, that meal in Vancouver.
...Trim the tops from some eggplant, make some small slashes in the body of the eggplant with a knife, and microwave for about 5 minutes.
...While the eggplant cook, add some canned tomatoes to a baking dish, breaking up the tomatoes with your hands if there are large chunks. ... Add about 2 tablespoons/30 ml of fried onions/shallots (I've been using fried shallots, as I was sent a can of fried shallots in oil).

item.title: How About a Nightcap?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
While not used much in modern times, I've recently become a fan of wearing a nightcap at night.
...In my own case, in recent times I've been sporting a shorter haircut and find that it can be cool at night to have less hair up on top. Our house does not have central heating per se, but we do have a wood stove to heat the house in winter.
...When I first thought of the nightcap last year, I was optimistic that finding a simple hat to wear at night would be easy.
...I also found the nightcap had the added benefit that, because it was loose and slid down partly over my face while sleeping, the nightcap also blocked light as morning slowly started emerging.

item.title: Christmas Poem, 2018
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It's nice to stop and pause
...we should all take the time
...then at least once, we should say
when we meet someone, soft and clear,
'Merry Christmas to you, and have a nice day!'

item.title: My December Garden
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
A quick look outside while I was having breakfast (after my morning walk) showed me how much green we still have in December.
...On the left, you can also see the stairs I built so that we can exit from the back of our house.
...It started growing in September and has a few tiny fruit growing, but I don't think we'll get much out of it this year.
...On the right side, in the raised bed in the foreground, there is garlic chives, kale and Swiss chard growing.
...Our tree at the back, in front of the wood shed will keep most of the leaves all winter, but will not sprout any new ones until the spring.

item.title: Beet Leaf Buns
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Sure, at some specialty shops you can sometimes find canned beets, but fresh beets are a rarity.
...Today at a farmer's market I found a few packages of fresh beets.
...I pickled the beets, boiled up the stems and will enjoy them over the next few days, but the leaves were the stars today.
Perhaps it comes from my Ukrainian background of wanting to be frugal and so using as much as possible of things from the garden. My mother would make this recipe and simple though it is, there is also some level of heavenly food within this recipe.

item.title: Influenza Vaccination
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
So, last weekend my wife and I got our annual influenza vaccinations, and afterwards I was wondering how things compared with other places.
...We fill in our personal information (name, age, address, and so on) and then are asked various questions about our current health.
...When we see the doctor (usually a wait of 5 minutes or so) he confirms what we are there for, takes our temperature and checks our general health.
...Then it's back out to the waiting room, and a few minutes later we are called to the desk and we pay.
...As we have many students of all ages, and I'm in contact with so many people all year, it seems like a good idea.

item.title: Thank you すっぱむーちょ
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
These chips were locally made and contained a variety of flavors, but my favorite was the Salt and Vinegar flavored ones.
My experience in Japan with potato chips is that while there are often some pretty interesting flavored chips offered from time to time, the usual flavors offered are often limited in nature.
...These recently purchased chips are labelled as a 25 year Thank-you product by the company on the bags of the chips. ... I feel that the Sour Mucho Strong chips were a bit more sour that these current chips, but this is just nitpicking.
...I know they will not be around long, and from what I've seen over the last few days, they are only found at very few stores.

item.title: CCES Halloween Baking Party
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It seems everyone and there dog (no offense to dogs) is having a Halloween party now, so we thought we'd change things up and have a Halloween Baking party.
...With so many colored icings and colored chocolate, who wouldn't go a bit overboard and have fun with the colors.
...Once the cookies were dripping with icing, we started on the most difficult part of the event, the 'Scary Rice Balls'. Using two pre-prepared rice balls as a guide, students decorated the rice balls to look like Frankenstein, using green rice, or to make a Skull, using pink rice. I hereby state that unequivocally, the students did a much better job than I in creating Frankenstein and Skull rice balls.

item.title: Pickled Peppers
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
So, using peppers from our garden and those graciously given from another friend, I was able to make these pickled peppers.
I simply made an incision into each pepper, tossed them into a pot with vinegar and salt, and let them boil for a couple of minutes.
Next, they were put into clean jars with a clove of garlic, and sealed.
In a few days, I'll try them and see whether we'll use them as is, or blend them into a sauce.
I'm keeping them in the fridge so there's no chance of spoilage.

item.title: Looking Good
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
It took me a while to get it done, but now that it is all over, I'm glad and impressed.
...One of the items I couldn't find was a gasket for the glass in the door. Last year I'd put on a gasket that wasn't the proper size, and didn't fit well, which meant that air was leaking into the wood stove, creating carbon on the glass, and making it look not nice.
...In a series of emails and late night phone calls (to deal with the time difference) over a one month period, I was finally able to have the company ship the item to me. In this day and age, when international business seems to be done effortlessly by most involved, there still exists those that are not up to speed.

item.title: My Magic Sauce
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I'm so happy what I have here (ooh yah, the Magic Sauce)
...I don't want to cause no fuss (ooh yah, the Magic Sauce)
...There was a BBQ sauce sold by the Real Canadian SuperStore in Winnipeg, where I lived that was unbelievably good.
...In my case, I found a recipe for a rib rub on-line that I liked and made that. Then, some of that was added to ketchup, and some vinegar, liquid smoke, and one or two other items added.

item.title: Home For a Rest
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
You'll have to excuse me I'm not at my best
...You'll have to excuse me I'm not at my best
