item.title: It's Time for a Rest
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The year starts in early January, and ends at the end of the year in December.
And now, after my university classes have finished and Japan is starting to celebrate the O-bon festival, I have a chance to take a break.
...Over the next few days, I won't be too busy with school things.
After my break, I'll be back to the grindstone.
I'll enjoy my break, and hopefully you'll be taking some break as well over the summer.

item.title: A Day in the Heat
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
For the last few weeks, our days start (6 AM) around 30C, and they end around the same temperature. ... If you haven't seen many posts (my last one was 19 days ago), it's because when it's this hot, you don't want to do much.
...After a siesta in the afternoon, I worked at splitting the last of the wood that I had. 2 hours later (hot), it was done.
...The flat breads were used with some sauce (my daughter made 2 types), some beef or chicken, and tomatoes and squash.
...The flat breads and meats were cooked outside on the BBQ, helping the keep the mosquitoes at bay and keep the house cool.

item.title: It's hammock time!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Now that the rainy weather seems to be finishing up, and the heat and sunshine seem here to stay, I decided to set up our hammock.
I had been laying peacefully for all of 2-3 minutes when Muffin looked outdoors, saw me, figured out that the hammock was back in action, and came out to join me.
...There is a gentle sway, that has the beneficial tendency to transport you to your days of being a baby rocked in someone's arms.
A light breeze would occasionally blow, and the hammock is just nice and comfortable.
Within 10 minutes I was out, having stopped reading my book and closing my eyes.

item.title: Rainy Season
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Usually, the rainy season where we live in Japan consists of days of rain/cloudy weather, then some nice weather, and then the pattern repeats, over and over for about 2 months.
It's never really clear when it starts (experts always announce the start and end, according to some information, but I think they just randomly pick dates) or when it ends. I say this because we usually can have about one week of straight rain and cloud and then the mighty weather soothsayers pronounce the beginning of the season.
...There have been multiple deaths over the last few days due to flooding, mudslides, and other events due to the rainy weather.
We have been lucky so far, and hopefully we should emerge from the rain with our homes and town intact; not so many other towns in Japan.

item.title: Sour Potato Chips: Joy of joys
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Salt and vinegar chips can be found in specialty stores, but the cost is often so high that I rarely buy them.
In Japan, common potato chip flavours often have a salty theme: salt flavoured, soy sauce flavoured, lightly salted flavoured, sea salt flavoured, and so on. Strong, different flavours can be found from time to time, but they often are made in small quantities and rarely become common place.
...The company produces other snack products that are sold at most stores, so it is strange that these sour chips are not sold everywhere.
I've purchased multiple bags of these chips because based on my prior experiences, products, even popular ones, have a tendency to disappear, never to return.

item.title: A Pound of Flesh
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I titled this a pound of flesh, but in actuality we bought a kilogram of plums, so it's more than a pound of flesh.
...Lately we've been enjoying using Japanese apricots for jam more than pickling them to make ume boshi.
When I spotted the apricots at the market yesterday we decided to buy some and make some jam.
...I could have cooked the jam further and given it more caramel-like flavors and colors, but I decided not to in the end.
...On the weekends when I have more time, I like to mix it with some garlic and soy sauce to make a glaze for chicken.

item.title: 2018 CCES Tacos Party
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We (our school) had our annual tacos party for the children students at our school.
It's a free event that gives students exposure to a different food from a different culture, and for most students this is their only opportunity to try a food such as this.
While not authentic by any means, we take baby steps in introducing this 'new' food to students. Hopefully the 'seed' will be planted in many of them, and perhaps in later years when there is an opportunity to try the real thing, they will be encouraged to do so.
...As a happy ending, there are usually leftovers from the party, and today is no exception.

item.title: Taste Testing: Clear Coffee
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I think the goal of this product is to give the essence of coffee, without the strong flavor and color elements.
...The taste is refreshing and clean, but you'd sort of expect that from a water product.
...I know that it is not coffee, and I know that it is not water, but when drinking it and tasting the coffee, you keep looking at the glass and checking what you're drinking.
I like the bitterness associated with coffee and other foods and drinks, but I also enjoy the taste of coffee when it is sweetened, such as an ice cream, cake or other dessert product.
...I can take some caffeine, but not too much so I like that aspect of this drink.

item.title: The Grass is Always Greener...
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
A lot of people around here like to build their houses as big as possible on their lot, and if there is any leftover space either have gravel or cement cover the remaining area.
...Over the years I've had many problems with our lawn, from neighborhood cats digging up newly planted sod to take care of their toiletry needs, to weeds or insects infesting our lawn.
A couple of years ago I finally ditched using the sod sold at home centres because it was a mesh-like product, and that once their were weeds inside it, became impossible to treat unless the entire piece of sod was removed.
...One of the weeds grew as a nice clump of green grass-like plant that would quickly send out seeds to produce more of it.
...At most places I went to for purchasing grass seed, the grass seed was sold in the same size packet that you usually find for planting carrots, or tomatoes, or any other number or garden plants.

item.title: Root Beer
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
One of the benefits (I'm guessing) for my mother working there was that she could take home a quart/litre of root beer each night, plus often a sandwich or two.
...When I came to Japan, I found that root beer is not only usually not available, but it is disliked by most people here in Japan.
...The taste often has a slight root beer flavor to it, and this is perhaps the source for many people here of the root beer taste. Yes, it is not the same, but it is similar (coincidentally, I find the taste of that medicine to be pretty good, though it is always consumed warm, and it lacks sweetness and bubbles).
...Today, when we opened the can (yes, only 1 can; A&W, if you're reading this, I would be happy, nay, overjoyed if you would send us free root beer) at lunch and shared it.

item.title: Happy Earth Day
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It's a good idea to help take care of our home, Earth, and to try to limit the damage done to it if we want to keep living here.
Today, my wife and I picked weeds from our parking lot by hand, instead of using any poisonous material which could harm plant foods or other living creatures.
We planted vegetables in our garden, and put more soil on our lawn to help the grass grow. Not many people around us have any lawn to speak of, but we think that besides looking nice, it keeps the area cooler in summer than concrete would.
...The Spring Rolls were delicious and we finished off our dinner with some carrot cake cupcakes, made from the carrots we were given.

item.title: Swirled Sesame Tea Cake
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I get a daily e-mail from their site and from time to time decide to make some of the recipes.
Sesame seeds have always tasted good to me, in almost any form, so I had a feeling I'd like this cake. ... There are no difficult instructions or ingredients involved so this is a good recipe for anyone who's interested to try.
In about 30 minutes, I had everything mixed up and the cake could go into the oven.
...I was actually struck by the fact that the sesame taste wasn't overpowering considering how much sesame seeds (and other versions of sesame seeds) went into it.

item.title: Pizza Muffins
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I decided that if there was tomato sauce, cheese and pepperoni together in one item, it would probably taste good, no matter what it was.
Last night as I was about to drift off to sleep, I was thinking about today's food, but realized that I'd have to make a decision. ... But, if I made the pizza muffins like pizza, using pizza dough, then it would be easier to mix up the dough and leave it to rise overnight.
...Thinking about how both items would taste (good, I thought), I decided to go with the pizza dough version, maybe because I like some difficulty in my life.
Out of bed I crawled, went to the kitchen (where one of my daughters happened to be making meringue cookies, matcha and chocolate, late on a Saturday night) to mix up the dough.

item.title: Why Body Shop, Why?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
You have to purchase a shaving brush, a shaving mug, the brush must be softened, the shaving cream soap must be mixed into a lather, and so on.
...As I write this blog on March 16th, 2018 I'm amazed that I was able to use it for almost a whole year, considering I shave on average 5 times a week.
...Recently, my visit to the only Body Shop in our city (well, not technically OUR city, since we live in Naruto and the store is in Tokushima, but I digress), I was going to purchase some more of their shaving cream only to find that they didn't have any. ... My feeling is that because they may not have many male customers, not much thought is ever given to the products used my males in the shop.
...My next visit back to Canada will include a visit to the Body Shop where I'll have to stock up on shaving cream.

item.title: Prepping for White Day
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
To remind you in case you forgot, White Day is yang or ying (I never know which is which) to Valentine's Day in Japan. Traditionally, females give something (usually chocolate) to males, and males are to reciprocate by giving something on White Day, March 14th.
This year I opted for white chocolate with pretzels, but wouldn't you know it, once I'd decided on an idea, pretzels became mostly non-existent here.
...Luckily my wife found some plain pretzels at a shop, and the pretzels were heart-shaped.
...Happily, the white-chocolate coated pretzel hearts taste great, greater than the sum, so I'm really pleased.

item.title: There is a Season
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The phrase may not be known to some of you, but for some of the more aware individuals, you'll recognize The Mamas and the Papas.
...I find that if I plant them a little closer to summer, they start growing and then slowly die off.
...I wouldn't think that it's too hot here, but there is something that prevents me from growing them in summer.
...I'm always amazed that cherry blossom season can begin here, yet there will still be many a night when we must keep using our wood stove to keep warm at night.
...I hope we can get a nice little crop of beans before the heat hits.

item.title: Garlic and Cilantro Soup with Chickpeas
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
This recipe for Açorda a Alentejana - Garlic and Cilantro Soup with Chickpeas - was downloaded from the Milk Street website.
...I've been regularly getting the free email news from Milk Street for awhile now, and occasionally recipes are available free to download from the site.
...Quickly this soup came together and the only major deviation from the original recipe was to add only one can, not two, of chickpeas.
...Lemony with garlic and cilantro, filling with bread cubes and chickpeas, and pleasing with balanced flavors and a hint of spice/heat after each spoonful, this is definitely a soup we will make again.
...I was fully sated from the big bowl I had, yet I could still eat the rest of our dinner (smoked BBQ salmon, creamed spinach, and rice).

item.title: Bike Shed - Finally Done!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Also, I wanted the wood to not rest on the ground, so that it wouldn't rot out too fast.
...The wood shed that I built last year is heavy enough, especially when full of wood, so that it's safe from the typhoons.
...After much hemming and hawing, I decided to use small blocks that came with metal bars imbedded in them, to which I attached the leggings.
...As with the wood shed made last year, the bike shed has been shingled, and all the wood has been treated with persimmon stain, which is natural and non-toxic. In the future, when the time comes to tear it down, I will not hesitate to use the wood in our wood stove, knowing that no toxic elements are in the wood.

item.title: Fruit Cocktail Cake
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
This simple dessert is one I discovered many years ago when working at a workplace that often had cooking as part of the duties. Not many of the staff liked to take on the task of cooking, but I was one of the few who relished the opportunity to play around in the kitchen. One of my co-workers was a great cook who didn't make any fancy recipes, but she her repertoire of basic recipes was quite huge and her food always tasted amazing.
...When I stopped off a a local supermarket on Friday while coming home from teaching at a university, I happened on a stack of fruit cocktail cans on sale, and this recipe immediately came to mind.
...But even cool, the cake is moist and delicious and it's hard not to eat seconds or thirds.

item.title: Gateway to a New Beginning
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Each day when I come back with Muffin from his walk, I'm required to step over the one meter fence, as untying it had become troublesome very quickly.
In recent years, I'd build a temporary wood shed made of wood re-claimed/recycled from the garbage wood leftover of a house being built. From one house, I was able to build the wood shed and then fill the shed and then some with the leftover wood.
...When I studied wood shops (as well as all of the other shops classes) in Junior high school, we didn't seem to have a lesson on building fences or gates.
...Luckily (really, really), my purchases at the local hardware store today (along with odds and ends leftover from other projects at the house) allowed me to salvage one piece of the old fence, add wheels to the bottom, hinges to the sides, and connect it to the aforementioned wood shed to become a new gate.

item.title: Behold the Simple Bagel
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Like many things, once something you like but take for granted is no longer available, you find yourself wanting it once again.
When I found myself in Japan many, many years ago, one of the things I found myself missing was good, simple bread. Oh, sure, there was bread in the city I came to (Tokushima) and it could be purchased almost everywhere I went. ... This bread is good for some things, but for me, it's not something I wish to eat everyday.
...I can remember when foreign English teachers at the school I worked at would go to a larger city (Fukuoka) for higher skill training.

item.title: Low and Slow
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Which is why, when recently we found during our weekly shopping trip (yes, we shop generally once a week, not every day, as we don't have the time to do so, and shopping every day can lead to spending more money than you have to) racks of pork ribs again for sale (they were sold last year for a while, and then disappeared with no sign of returning).
...Having never cooked ribs when I lived in Canada, they quickly became one of those foods I suddenly craved because they are so hard to find here.
...Because I've bought these ribs a couple of times in the past (when I've found them), I now have some experience cooking them.
...I had to do a bit of searching for recipes, but I finally found one that made a really good rub, and what's more, the same mixture could be used to create a BBQ sauce, which we've used not only with ribs, but with other cooking.
...Next, the ribs went on the grill where I had only a small amount of charcoal burning, with an added chunk of cherry wood for some smoke.

item.title: Ginger Beer
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Yet my journey has often been a lonely one, and while I felt safe and confident in my journey, there were always questions that would pop up.
...However, the more I read, the more I realize how right I was to be doing this all my life, and how I want to do even more.
To be honest, at first I was a little disappointed that the book was not more like a cookbook with recipes laid out with easy to follow instructions. But the more I read of the book, I realized that fermentation is a fluid activity, something I'd already figured out with beer-making and bread-making, and thus, the recipes given in the book made perfect sense.
...Since that first time at the end of the summer, I've now made ginger beer several times and have loved it thoroughly each time.

item.title: New Stairs
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Not so for my Dad, who then had to find out what was wrong with the machine and set about fixing it.
...Earlier this year, at the beginning of summer I noticed that our outside stairs/steps had some boards loose that needed to be replaced.
...Well, the summer finished and lately I took another look at the stairs and decided I'd have to start fixing them, as soon as the weather was OK.
Finally, I had free time and the weather cooperated, so I determined that there were a few boards that were rotten and I'd replace them.
...Another hours work and somehow I came up with a plan to rebuild the stairs, plus some of the boards pieced together.

item.title: Necessity is the Mother of...Spanakopita
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Recently I've been reading an old issue of Saveur Magazine, my mother's copy actually, that I brought back from Canada a few years ago.
...After a recent shopping trip on Amazon.com, I was the proud owner of a container of feta cheese.
...Feta is rarely seen here, and when seen it is often in very small containers and with herbs. Phyllo is rarely seen over here, though occasionally can be bought from different sources over the internet.
There was much chopping, rolling and baking, and the spanakopita came out of the oven all golden brown.

item.title: Good-bye Summer, Hello Fall
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
My oldest daughter and I baked this up yesterday, and today I finally had a piece (yesterday my wife and younger daughter made 2 delicious loaves of chocolate banana bread, so that's what I had last night).
As I've recounted before, I didn't care too much for pumpkin pie when I lived in Canada, though I did eat it from time to time.
...Firstly, here in Japan I always use Kabocha squash (though it is like pumpkin) instead of the pumpkin or canned pumpkin used in North America (which truth be told is watery and not very tasty, in my opinion).
...While I'd offer you a taste, you'd have to get here pretty darned quick because once we start slicing the pie, it doesn't last for long.
...Fall is upon us, and what better way to ring in the start of the season, but with a nice slice of pie.

item.title: Back on the (Woodsplitter) Horse
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes I would lightly hold the wood to make sure the wood wouldn't move from the position I'd put it in.
...Well, a few weeks ago, I had my hand on top of the wood, resting it there and holding the wood to prevent it from turning.
...OK. I've experienced this before (once on the same thumb, when I hit my thumb accidentally with a hammer while I was splitting wood, once on the other thumb when skiing in Canada).
...I was told that there was a great chance of infection due to the fact that blood had come out; while it was not bleeding externally very much, there was a great chance it was bleeding internally.
...I'm happy to report that all my fingers and toes are OK. I made a promise to myself and my wife that I would never ever touch the wood on the wood splitter again, but if needed would use some tool to touch the wood.

item.title: Some Ethiopian Food
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
But let's be clear: this book was published in the 1990's, and at that time in Canada and even I'm guessing the United States, there was not the widespread availability of foods that exists today.
...Some novels I've read over the years which mention Ethiopian food make me think that the food is often spicier than how I prepare it. ... While it may be easier to find in North America now that it was in the 1990's, here in Naruto, Japan it is non-existent.
...Two major sauces are required for most of the recipes; the sauces are easy to make but require many ingredients and also take some time to make.
...If you have access to Ethiopian foods or a market, feel free to send me some of them as a present.

item.title: FlexSolar Portable Solar Charger
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
With all the devices that have crept into our lives, I'm always a little concerned about the amount of energy needed to keep everything going.
So, when I saw this solar charger being sold on http://www.kickstarter.com/ I decided to become a backer of the project and invest my money.
...One of the things I liked about the solar charger was that is is waterproof; another is that it folds up to almost the size of my smartphone.
I can charge my devices directly from the solar panel, or I can charge the power bank, then connect it to my devices.
Now, it is true that the charging is not as fast as just plugging your devices, via cables, into electrical outlets.

item.title: Woodshed: Finished
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Home-centres, as they are referred to here in Japan are supposed to be places for the weekend warrior of home-improvement to get their goods.
...The home-centres I visited (2 out of 3) offered one type of asphalt shingle, but an inferior version of what I'd used before. ... When I showed a picture of the shingles I'd used before to staff at one home-centre, I was told that these were shingles for the professional and so they didn't have the (superior version) shingles I was looking for.
This was strange, because when I did web-searches for asphalt shingles in Japan, often home-renovation companies would show a picture of an individual installing the very type of shingle I wanted to buy, but was unavailable.
...We had to play e-mail tag for a while, but the goods finally came in a reasonable amount of time, and the shingles were good.

item.title: うめ/Japanese Apricot Jam
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I've said this before (see my post about making this jam some years ago) but people should really try making this jam.
It's dead easy, due to all the pectin in the apricots. ... Remove the apricot pits at some point (psssst - they taste delicious as well; don't just throw them out).
...You see, most people will use Japanese apricots/梅/うめ/ume to make the familiar and delicious ume boshi (梅干し), the famous pickle often referred to as pickled plum, and often a dark red colour due to being flavoured and coloured with red shiso leaves.
...But if you fly over this weekend, you'll still be able to find loads of them in stores.

item.title: How do you cook your 竹の子/bamboo shoots?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We have a neighbour, bless his heart, that gives us fresh 竹の子 / bamboo shoots that he's just dug up in the mountain.
Today's batch of bamboo shoots are slimmer than the ones we see earlier in the Spring, but no doubt they'll be just as tasty.
...After carefully opening up the shoot and peeling off the outer leaves, the inner shoot is cut into smaller pieces and placed in a pot. ... If you don't have any rice bran, you can add some uncooked rice and use that. Right now I'm slowing cooking it, so I have to run to the kitchen every few minutes to make sure it isn't bubbling over, even though it is on a low simmer.

item.title: 2017 Tacos Party
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Yes, today we welcomed our younger students to our home to make tacos, at our annual Tacos Party.
There isn't a large selection of international food here in Naruto, so I always enjoy introducing the younger students to tacos, a food from another culture.
...Over the years, doing our 'Tacos Party' we've introduced this food to lots and lots of kids who would have never had the opportunity to try the food otherwise.
...As usual, the students were 'tacos masters' at making their flour tortillas in no time flat. In fact the youngest member (this being her second time to join this party in as many years) kept urging me to let them at the dough while I did my demonstration of how to make the tortillas.

item.title: Happy Birthday, Muffin!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Of course he's much larger now than he was back then, and he's quite the handsome guy.
Each day Muffin begins with a 30-minute walk around town, checking the latest gossip at various 'watering' spots, as well as getting some exercise.
He loves to play with his toys (sometimes even allowing us to join in the activities), chew on his various bones and antlers, sleep, and hang out with us.
Muffin celebrated his birthday today with some bbq'd chicken breast for dinner, and a birthday muffin (appropriately chosen) made with carrots and other yummy things.
We think he enjoyed his birthday events today and likely he'll have a lot of pleasant dreams tonight.

item.title: Self-serve Food Kiosks
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Around town, and I assume around Japan, you may find these kiosks on streets selling a variety of homegrown or home-prepared goods.
While I've usually only seen food for sale, I do know of one kiosk that sells bags of composted soil for about 100 yen.
Some of the kiosks only sell one type of goods (for example, around here you may find kiosks selling only lotus roots or sweet potatoes), while others sell a variety of goods.
...No change is available, so you must have exact change, or you should pay more if you don't have exact change (for example, paying with a 500 yen coin when purchasing 400 yen worth of goods).
...However it's good to believe in the good nature of people and trust that most people will pay for the goods.

item.title: Woodshed: Some Progress
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Today, after going swimming (my health is important) and making dough and sauce for pizza tonight (pizza is important, too!), I found a bit of time to devote to the woodshed project.
As can be seen, the flooring is now almost complete, and I purchased wood for the corner posts.
If the weather cooperates next weekend, I should be able to get all the posts on and perhaps even some of the top.
I continue to find leftover wood from various construction sites, but I still have to find cut trees to use for firewood later this year.
Luckily I don't have any wood right now as I don't have the space to keep it.

item.title: Woodshed: Work Continues
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I took advantage of the nice weather (and no work) to continue my work on our woodsheds.
Previously we had 2 woodsheds but I'm going to try to make four connected woodsheds. A few weeks ago I had finished the floor of one of the sections, but today I was able to complete the remaining sections.
...I still don't know how I'm going to make the roof section in the corner, but that's for another day.
Today I'm glad that I could triple the amount of work I had done on the sheds.

item.title: A Bird in the Hand...
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We have a very small back yard and due to the extreme angle I'm not able to see to the very top of houses from back there, but the songs seem to be coming from the rooftops.
...Many pictures of pop bottle bird feeders seem to show a couple of wooden spoons used for holding the seed from the feeder, and providing a perch for birds. The site I used for inspiration suggested that I could use some leftover wooden spoons I have lying around my house. I'm not sure who happens to have 'leftover' wooden spoons just lying around the house and not being used for cooking, but this situation doesn't apply to us.
...Should you know any birds in need of sustenance, please let them know that dinner is on us if they make it on over here.

item.title: Woodshed Salvage Work
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
From the wood used to build the woodsheds, some of it was salvaged for new framing in our outdoor shed. We had been using particle board bookshelves in the shed, but I felt it wasn't working properly for storing our goods.
...Some of the wood salvaged was burned in our wood stove and the rest (that which was painted with wood stain) has been cut up and thrown in the garbage. ... The 2x4's that I won't burn in my wood stove will be burned in the city's garbage facility.
Finally, the bricks that will be used for the foundation of the new woodsheds have been put into place and levelled, and I have slowly begun the process of building the new woodshed.

item.title: Woodshed, De-constructed
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Many moons ago, with wood salvaged from packing crates that were destined for the garbage bin, I put together my second woodshed, as my first one was constantly full.
...Over the years, I've noticed a little deterioration in the woodsheds and decided that this year I should replace them both with one bigger woodshed (I still don't know how I'm going to make that one - suggestions welcomed).
Today I got down to taking apart this woodshed, and also seeing how I built it in the first place.
...Only some of the wood at the bottom was starting to rot out, though if I had wanted, I could have replaced the bad sections with newer wood.
The newer woodshed, whenever it is built will be slightly different in design, but very similar to the original models; perhaps a bit taller, perhaps a bit bigger, but mostly the same.

item.title: The Problems with Beef Jerky in Japan
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I received a call recently from the good people at the Customs Bureau in Japan informing me that the package (Christmas) I was expecting had arrived, but that some offensive articles would be removed.
...To my knowledge, American and Canadian beef products had been cleared of any dangerous classifications in recent years (especially as, like I said, the same sort of product can be found in some stores).
...It seems that while American and Canadian beef products are acceptable in Japan, regulations are so complicated that it becomes quite difficult for individuals to get such products for private consumption in Japan.
...I first considered sending the items back to Canada, but having not yet sent back the letter with my choice, decided to phone and ask a bit more about this.
...When I asked about who would pay to return the goods, I was told that I would have to phone the Post Office in Tokyo to determine who would be paying for the return, and that the customs office would definitely NOT pay.

item.title: Tis the Season to Eat Nabe
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I've extolled the virtues of Nabe before, so I won't go into that story today.
We're still in the midst of winter here, and while not as cold as many other places, it is still cold for us here.
...There are so many variations on the dish so there is usually something for everyone's lifestyle.
Tonight we enjoyed Sesame-Miso flavoured Nabe that included various vegetables, tofu and sliced pork. ... Leftovers will be eaten tomorrow for lunch and the flavours will be just as good, if not better.

item.title: A Sampling from bakery nook in Naruto
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
When I came to Japan, many moons ago, finding bread that was not soft, white, tasteless sandwich-style bread was a challenge.
...Previously, as I understand it, this bakery was baking goods by special order, and also appearing at various markets selling their goods.
...We sampled a chocolate bagel, which contained pieces of chocolate and almond inside, a strawberry bread which looks white but smells and tastes, mildly, of strawberry, and a small french bread, wee in size but big in flavour.
...Staff were friendly, and very surprising was that they keep a pot of coffee on hand for customers to enjoy, for free. ... While I do enjoy regular coffee, such as espresso in the mornings, I do not want the caffeine that comes with regular coffee on many days, and it is impossible for me to drink it in the afternoon or evening without it affecting my sleep.

item.title: Twas the Night Before Christmas
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
What they typed and swiped, while they blocked out the tree.
The rice cooker was set, to make up the white stuff
...I ran to the door to see what was the matter.
...I hoped the rest of the night would not make a peep.
...I wished for a good night and Happy Christmas to all!

item.title: Tokushima LED Art Festival 2016
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
In various places throughout the city of Tokushima, the company teamLab had created a wide assortment of illumination that allowed the viewer to not only enjoy viewing the illumination, but also at times interacting with it.
...Over the course of a few hours, my daughter's iPod registered that we'd walked over 6000 steps during our viewing of the various instalments found around the city.
...One of the things I like best about winter is when there are things for people to go out and do and enjoy themselves, rather than staying inside.
...Highlights of the festival for me were the giant luminous balls that were floating in and around the Shinmachi River that kept changing colours, the dancing Awa Dancers wearing special LED costumes, the giant 'Christmas tree' made out of thousands of LEDs that users could add decorations to, using their smartphones, and finally the forest of trees that communicated with us, via sound and light, pictured above in the video.
Should you find yourself in the vicinity of Tokushima, Japan over the next few days, take the time to enjoy this festival.

item.title: Persimmon Chutney
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Like a lot of produce, there are times when there is none, and there are times when there is almost too much. We don't own a persimmon tree, but we sometimes buy them at stores and markets to enjoy eating them as is.
...Chutney is not very popular here, and while it can be bought, it can be a little expensive. One of the most common chutneys is mango chutney, but we don't have access to lots of mangoes.
...I threw in some onion, apple, raisins, spices including coriander and cumin, lemon peel, chopped jalapeños, sugar and vinegar and cooked it all up.

item.title: Halloween Party 2016
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Pictured above are some of the guests at our annual Halloween party, making mummies.
...We had a variety of events that had everyone, from the youngest to the oldest guests involved.
There were great costumes and make-up, funny events and scary experiences, and of course candy and sweets.
Thanks to everyone who helped with the event and also those who attended. We look forward to next year's party!

item.title: Smoked Salmon Spread, a la もくさくえき
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
One of the things I like to treat myself with when I go back to visit Canada is some Smoked Salmon Cream Cheese. Not only myself, but the rest of my family also loves it, and so it quickly disappears when we bring back some to Japan.
...Using some cream cheese, a can of salmon (not flaked), and some liquid smoke I was able to make a good spread.
...I let the flavour deepen overnight in the refrigerator and we had it the next morning at breakfast with toast.
...Because it was easy to make and I still have a lot more of my liquid smoke, we'll be enjoying this many times more in the future.

item.title: Sudachi Pie
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
We usually make a lot of juice and slowly drink the juice with water and sugar.
A few years ago I made a meringue pie with Sudachis, but this year I decided to make something different.
I followed the basic recipe for making Key Lime Pie but used Sudachis instead of Key Limes.
Thankfully we still have more Sudachi juice in our fridge because this pie disappeared pretty quickly.
For those of you living in Tokushima, here's another delicious way to use your Sudachis.

item.title: Sloppy Joes
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Years ago in Canada, I usually made Sloppy Joes by buying the flavouring packet that you added to your meat and vegetables and in minutes you had a tasty dinner ready.
Here in Japan, I'm guessing that while that Sloppy Joes mix might exist somewhere, it is not common and not worthwhile searching for on my part.
...While eating this food, the sauce has a tendency to drip out of the bun and make a mess, hence the name 'Sloppy' Joes.
...So, I made up my Sloppy Joes, adjusting my recipe here and there and they turned out great. I decided for my first helping to use a half bun with sauce, twice, instead of eating it like a hamburger.

item.title: A Little Slice of Heaven
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Crosswords, Scrabble, Word searches, Jumbles, Sudoku (not a word game, but in the same group I think) are all things I like to do.
...From time to time, I will get newspapers or newspaper clippings from Canada that is the crosswords, word puzzles, comics, or sudoku from the paper. ... Not only do I get to do a puzzle of some sort, but the other side of the paper will have some tidbit of news from abroad, whether it is an obituary, sales advertisement, or piece of news.
Announcement to anyone from abroad reading this blog: should you have finished your newspaper and have no further need of it, why not recycle it by sending it to me, care of my school (address is found on our homepage).
Sending your old newspapers to me will help the environment because we will be recycling and reusing the product, and I will get a chance to do more puzzles!

item.title: I've got a pocket full of...
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Surprisingly, my pockets could hold quite a few olives before I had to head back to my car and find a bag to put them into.
I'm happy that I could find some this year because I've been looking here and there all summer and there haven't been very many in our city.
...I found a few around town, but they were at the tops of very tall trees, all but impossible to get access to. I gave up and for the first time in about a decade was unable to pickle any olives for our consumption.
Yesterday when I found the olives I knew that I would have preferred to wait a few more weeks for them to ripen more, but with a few typhoons in the area and bad weather forecast for the next 3+ days, I decided to pick the olives and make due with them.

item.title: Waiting for Mommy
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
'Mommy' refers to my wife and does not mean that she is the mother of our dog. While some people refer to themselves as the mother or father of their dogs, we do not.
...Muffin cares deeply about everyone in the family and he's showing his devotion today.
My wife was out of the house for the day and for the first hour or so, Muffin stayed near the entrance of the house because 'something was not right with the universe.'
...It's guess it's tough being a dog, but we're always glad and grateful we've Muffin in our family.

item.title: Neighbourhood Cats, Beware!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I've lived only in Tokushima city and Naruto city for my 20+ years in Japan, so my experience is limited to these areas.
...While I have never had cats of my own, I have cared for numerous cats for friends and family years ago in Canada and enjoyed doing so.
...Around our fine town, I often see signs warning dogs (I think dog owners, since I assume most dogs would not read the signs) not to use the area for their toiletry needs.
...Over the last few months, again we've had to contend with filling bags and bags of toiletry waste from cats, as well as regurgitated animals (mice, birds).
...If you have better suggestions for dealing with these cats, or if you'd like to take any of these homeless cats home with you and help alleviate my problem, please contact me.

item.title: In Search of Smoke
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I've also sent this to family in Canada and they rave about it being so much better than any similar product they have found in Canada.
I'm not embarrassed to say that we got lost on our way, but for that I put part of the blame on my phone's GPS.
...If your map reading skills are better than mine, you can always just look at Mr. Hayashi's homepage where you will find loads of details and pictures about his products.
We were warmly greeted by Mr. Hayashi and his wife, were given some recently harvested produce, given a tour of their property including an explanation of the production and of the final products.
We enjoyed hearing information about the products and decided in the end to not only buy liquid smoke, but also some charcoal for using to BBQ with and some charcoal to use in the house and car to help with the air quality.

item.title: BBQ'd Pizza, Re-visited
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It's amazing how quickly the pizza cooks and how different the end result is from pizza baked in our oven.
...As I stated last year in my blog, you have to move quickly when cooking pizza on the BBQ.
...Both sides of the pizza get charred spots, adding some smokiness to the final taste, and the crust becomes very crispy.
This pizza (one of many we had) was topped with roasted red pepper (roasted with the charcoal as the charcoal was getting ready), dry sausage, pineapple, cheese and basil.
...But look I will, and I will remember and hopefully soon, we'll re-visit BBQ'd pizza again.

item.title: Fireworks/Hanabi/花火
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
This is because the date in Japanese (ha-8月=August; na= 7th; bi-日=day) reads the same as the word fireworks (hanabi/花火, literally 'flower of fire').
...I'm not sure how many people visit, or how it ranks with other shows, but it seems to be the largest one in this area of Japan. Living here (we are literally 5-10 minutes walking from the site) we don't have to deal with the traffic jams, which I understand can be quite long both before and especially after the show.
And, as beautiful as today's show was (and is, every year) I can't help but always think about the novel, The Day of the Triffids, by John Wyndham.
...Thus, overtime I watch fireworks, a part of me wonders whether tomorrow morning, myself and others will be blinded by what we all enjoyed.

item.title: RELAQ - Good Place for a Workout
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
While I can do some different exercises at home, recently I felt it was important to get out of the house so I wouldn't have any excuse for not working out. Getting out of the house means that I'm committed to doing something, which is just the sort of motivation I was looking for.
Another reason I wanted to do exercises away from my home was that I have very little equipment at home for exercising.
...I was given great advice about exercises to do and how to do them, as well as explanations about how to use the equipment available.
...Should you be in need of toning up your body, or getting into good, physical shape, then I suggest you join me on weekends and see what a great place RELAQ can be for you.

item.title: Channelling My Inner Mom
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
In the morning after breakfast, I went out and, using the chainsaw, cut up a pile of wood that I'd recently picked up.
...Next, I cleaned up the piles of old sod that I'd removed earlier this summer, when I pulled out the old sod (which was full of weeds) and re-seeded the area with new grass seed. ... The old sod was full of weeds, but also full of soil, was heavy, and there was a lot of it. We've had a lot of rain recently due to the annual rainy season weather, so it was difficult to finish this before.
...She did loads of laundry, cleaned rooms in the house, vacuumed, dusted, threw out old, unnecessary items, mopped the floors, went shopping, and did yard work.

item.title: Hey, Neighbours, Happy Independence Day!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I just got through talking with my students about Canada Day (July 1st) and explaining what Canadians do and who we are.
...So I thought, why not combine both events in one stroke and decided to cook up some Butter Tart Slice.
...This recipe is a lazy way of making the same thing, as it cooks up as one giant slice which can be cut into individual pieces (if you decide to share with others).
One of the ways Americans may celebrate Independence Day is with a BBQ with all sorts of good foods to eat.
I offer my Butter Tart Slice as the dessert portion of your celebration, in addition to whatever else you've prepared.

item.title: Damn you, BBC.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Unfortunately, weak people like myself can quickly become overcome with a desire to cook and/or eat the food that's being discussed in this series of stories.
So it was with last week's story about samosas in India.
After reading the story, I planned samosas as one of the upcoming week's menu items, made sure we had the necessary ingredients, and then earlier this week I set about trying to make them.
I cut corners by using large wonton wrappers instead of making the dough, knowing that I was going to be busy this week.
Due to my shortcut and lack of skill, I wasn't able to get the proper shape of the samosa.

item.title: Done for Another Year
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Finally I was able to cross off the item 'clean the wood stove chimney' from my To Do list (I don't have any such list).
In Spring, the weather gets warmer and we have the odd fire at night to take the chill out of the house, and then at some point you realize 'we are done having fires in the wood stove for this year.'
...While it's possible to clean the chimney when it rains, I prefer not to because sometimes rain is blown into our chimney and part of the cleaning process involves cleaning some parts outside.
...Years ago, when I first bought my chimney cleaning supplies in Canada I had the misfortune of dealing with a jerk of a salesperson who questioned every product I wanted to buy. Living in Japan, it wasn't easy for me at the time (and it still isn't that easy today) to pick up supplies for our wood stove.

item.title: I've Got a Bone to Pick With You
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
You think of 'meat' as 'meat', with no concern about what it is you're eating, or where it came from (not place, but animal).
...Oh, you can find the odd piece of meat (chicken legs) that has bones, but by and large the bones have been removed from the meat before it is displayed.
...Of course we bought some, because another experience I know only too well is that sometimes interesting foods will appear in supermarkets here, only to magically disappear and never again show up.
...It was a good feast today and I hope I will be able to purchase ribs in the future here, but I never know if that will be the case.
If only Adam's Ribs existed, and could deliver to Japan, life would be easier - as long as I remembered to order the coleslaw.

item.title: Red Shiso Extract / 赤しそエキス
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
The red variety is used to colour Japanese apricots to make the famous accompaniment to rice, ume boshi / pickled plum (though it isn't a plum) / 梅干し. I don't see it used as much as the green variety, so for that reason we don't grow the red version.
...My wife however saw red shiso at the market the other day and purchased it, not for making pickles of any sort, but for making red shiso extract. My memory isn't what it used to be, but I do remember she also made some last year and it quickly disappeared.
...When you drink this extract with some soda and ice, you taste the shiso (delicious), you taste the vinegar (a bit tart), you taste the sugar (sweet) and you taste the love.

item.title: Whole-Wheat Sourdough Bread
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I've been making bread for years now, and in recent years I've often made a lot of no-knead bread.
As good as that bread is (and I will continue to make it) it seemed I should also start to make bread using a real sourdough, gathering yeasts from nature instead of using store-bought yeast.
The model for Micheal Pollan's bread is Chad Robertson, an American baker in San Francisco who's been making natural sourdough's for quite a long time now.
...However, when you mix large portions of flour and water together it seems like having some air in there will make for a lighter and hopefully tastier food.
...And so it is with this bread, as at dinner time members of my family who like white soft fluffy bread were happy to enjoy slice after slice of this loaf.

item.title: Proverb: Many hands make for...
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
When I came to Japan, Mexican food was one of those things that was really difficult to find in this neck of the woods.
...Oh, sure, you can find the odd bit of Mexican food here and there, but generally this food type has never really caught on in this part of Japan (and maybe in many parts of Japan).
I do my small part of introducing others to this delicious food by hosting an annual Tacos Party for the younger students at our school every spring/summer.
...But I'm even happier when I announce the upcoming party each year, and knowing students smile, nod their heads and say that tacos are delicious!
...Hopefully these students will grow up and if they ever happen upon a shop selling tacos, they'll recall their experiences here and a smile will appear on their face (as well as a tummy-rumbling, and the thought that they'd better order some tacos!)

item.title: Rum Raisin Pie
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I've heard that there are some people who don't like raisins, and that's too bad.
...Perhaps it wasn't too good for our teeth (as we didn't usually brush them after eating raisins) but it was a natural snack packed with energy and nutrients for our bodies.
...Thus, the pie I made today, one that my mother made from time to time is a simple raisin pie with the addition of some rum.
...Each mouthful contained raisins that had swelled with liquid (including some of that rum) that popped in your mouth while eating the pie.
Thankfully there is some pie leftover which I will be able to snack on tomorrow as well.

item.title: Braised Venison
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I have been lucky enough to have eaten quite a lot of it in my past life in Canada.
...Here in Japan, I've also been lucky in knowing farmers who've killed deer on their farms and have shared the deer meat. The meat is fresh, wild, and free of commercial feeding, having lived in the wild and often having eaten food grown by farmers.
...I braised the venison long and slow, meaning that it took hours (and hours) to cook, but it was cooked at a very low temperature.
...However, my feeling is that within the next 24 hours, a lot of the meat will disappear (along with it's gravy) meaning that by Monday when some of us will need weekday lunches, there may not be a lot of it available.

item.title: ASUS Zenfone 2 Laser ZE550KL
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
When we recently reached the point of having to purchase a smartphone for one of our daughters, we did research and followed recommendations and eventually settled on the ASUS Zenfone 2 Laser 550KL.
...Yet, it seems that after using said smartphone for a while, my daughter's one complaint was about the size: it was kind of big.
...Prior to its purchase, we asked our daughter whether she'd prefer to keep her phone, or instead take my new phone which would be smaller, but have less features.
...I love the sense of freedom I have with this phone and the idea that I can use it anywhere with any company (well, not with anything Apple-related).
...With these fees, I'm paying about the same as I paid for my old phone which only really about me to make phone calls and send the most basic of messages.

item.title: Dill Buns
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Luckily our dill plants have survived all through the winter and now that there is warmer weather they are getting tall and bushy.
With all the beautiful dill in the garden and not a cucumber in sight in the garden, my thoughts wandered back to memories of my mother's dill and cottage cheese buns.
I made these buns from time to time, but I often use my mother's other filling of ground meat.
...The dill and cheese buns were usually made with cottage cheese by my mother, but cottage cheese is very expensive where I live in Japan (and I'm guessing the same is true for most parts of Japan).
...But I'll probably start looking for some cheap cucumbers to make some fresh dill pickles with in the next few days.

item.title: Pickled Easter Eggs
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Many of the Easter decorations I have up on my walls and windows for Easter show colourful Easter eggs.
...Beets can be difficult for me to find, and so I've got my own supply of processed beet juice concentrate for when I need to make some Borscht. The beet juice is processed (cooked) so the colour isn't as beautiful as the juice from fresh or canned beets, but it still is purple-y and the taste is good.
...This is the first time for me to try the curried pickled eggs and I love the colour and taste of them. Next year (I've done enough for this year) I think I'll try some chili pickled eggs, and maybe some spinach wasabi pickled ones.

item.title: Hot Cross Buns (sort of)
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Yet my memories of Easter stray more towards the Easter ham, and the (drool) fantastic sandwiches we'd eat for days after with the leftover ham.
...I don't celebrate much of Easter here in Japan because I'm not very religious and it's difficult to get a nice ham or lamb for dinner (I'm into food in case you haven't noticed).
...The package had more than enough fruit for my recipe and I've kept the leftover waiting to use it for some other recipe.
I knew I'd be making some Hot Cross Buns, and rather than adding the usual fruits and spices, I decided to go the whole nine yards and add in the leftover fruit/spice mixture, which has all the fruits I need plus extras to my recipe for the buns. The buns baked up nice and fluffy, full of spice and sweetness, yet not overly sweet like cinnamon buns can be (though I do like ton indulge in them as well at times).

item.title: What's on the Menu? Grilled Sardines
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
The smells must be incredible for him, plus he gets the odd chunk of food off of the grill as a favour for his special 'BBQ guard duty' while we do grilling.
...The first time I had grilled sardines was many a moon ago at the Folkorama Festival in my hometown of Winnipeg.
I can remember being so surprised, because up to that point in my life I didn't care for sardines, and sardines were a canned fish that some people (not me) ate in sandwiches. To this day I can remember the smokey, BBQ-y, oily, sardine that I bought, and how delicious it was.
...The sardines were smaller than the ones I remember and because of my use of smoking wood chips tasted different.

item.title: Tandoori Chicken Burgers
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）

My job (Conversational English Teacher) allows me to do a lot of my work from home meaning that I can do quite a bit of cooking.

...Muffin, my daughter and I sampled the odd little bits of chicken that stuck to the BBQ grates, or that stuck out from the burgers and we concluded that they tasted pretty good.
...The pickles were sour/salty, with bits of mint and cilantro flavouring, the sauce made with the same herbs was cool and herbal, the meat was smoky, with tandoori spices adding flavour and a touch of heat, and finally the naan which was pillowy soft and buttery but also a touch smoky from being on the BBQ.

item.title: Prepping for White Day

item.title: Difficulties of High School Entrance in Japan
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Of course, most children finish high school and even go to university, but it's not required that they enter high school.
Children, important as they are, even more so here in Japan where the population is rapidly diminishing, seem to be in a continual schooling battle.
...To enter your chosen high school, if your scores are high enough, your teachers may write a letter of recommendation allowing you to enter the high school.
...But there are times where a student may choose to ignore the schools' recommendation and try for a school that may be beyond their capabilities. The students may hope that their scores on one of the special entrance tests may be high enough to enter, and also hope that there will be a spot available for them to enter the school.

item.title: Tonight's Dinner - Thai-ish Food
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
The temperatures are cool - not cold mind you - but cool and with the rain, it was a damp, dark day.
Our cilantro survived the snow scare earlier this year and we thought today could be a good time to use some of it.
I'm not sure where I picked up these recipes, but they come from a variety of cookbooks and cooking magazines and combine for a nice dinner.
We had a beef salad on a bed of greens, rice noodles with a peanut and chili paste sauce, and a salad or slaw made with a variety of vegetables and herbs.
...Tummy is happy, mind is happy, we're happy; isn't that a nice way to finish off the day?

item.title: Chanko-Nabe/ ちゃんこ鍋
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Looking back at my life in Canada before I came to Japan, one of the things that surprises me is that I ate Nabe, or Japanese stew in Canada.
...I can't recall what kind of Nabe I ate in Canada (blame the copious bottles of Sake we drank), but it was enjoyed.
...Nabe basically involves making a broth (which can be simple or complex-tasting) and then adding other ingredients, all fresh, and cut to bite-size portions, letting it cook together for a short time, and then eating it in small bowls, either as is or with various sauces. Nabe is usually cooked in a clay pot over a portable gas burner at the table-side, allowing guests to eat and cook all during the meal.
...The rice cooks in the broth that previously had the vegetables and/or meats and/or seafood, soaking up all those flavours.

item.title: When it rains...or in this case, snows...
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
When you say snow, and lots of it, and you're scared of it, you have to remember that our experiences with the white stuff are different. Having lived here in Japan on the island of Shikoku for 20 years, I can speak fairly well about the chance of this part of world having any 'scary snow experience.'
...As it was cold this morning, and has continued to be cold (by Shikoku's standards), we've had our wood stove burning up some of that wood I collected last year, making our house nice and toasty warm.
Since I had the wood stove going, and since we'll have pizza for dinner tonight, I decided to do some prep work.
...While I could cook the pizzas in the wood stove, it can be difficult to get bigger foods in and out of the wood stove.

item.title: Dog Biscuits
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Recently I've been using breadsticks as a snack for him because they were cheap (about $1) and they didn't have salt or oil.
...I thought the dog biscuits weren't hard enough and contained some questionable ingredients, and the cheese-flavoured breadsticks sounded tasty but were rather expensive.

...Seeing as how I made them and they had no bad ingredients, I did some testing with Muffin and found them pretty good. I'll save them for Muffin though, seeing as I have other options to munch on and he doesn't.

item.title: Thoughts on Wood Stoves From My Dad
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It takes a lot of work to maintain the wood stove's condition. It takes a lot of work, and money to get all the wood. ... There's also dangers with hurting yourself (I've broken 2 fingers in the past) and with fire damaging something.
...I don't know when it was written or why (we never had a wood stove in Canada) but I understand the deeper meaning of the note more than most.
...I haven't made it to the coffee table stage yet, and I'm still married, so I'm thankful.

item.title: 大掃除 / Big End of Year Cleaning
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Baking goodies takes weeks to prepare (no complaining, as there is lots of 'testing' the baked cookies, slices, cakes, sweets, etc. to make sure everything is up to snuff).
...Again, I don't mind because we can enjoy the food for a couple of days and so I do less cooking after Christmas.
...One of the traditions I learned when I came to Japan was that before New Year's Day, families like to clean their house so that the new year starts with a nice, clean house.
...For us, cleaning generally involves cleaning the kitchen: all the cabinets, inside and out, same with the refrigerator, throwing out old foods/spices, and cleaning the overhead vent/fan.
...It's nice to get rid of that layer of dust, the piece of clothing I never wear anymore, the grime in the kitchen, and the spots on the windows.

item.title: Hungarian Paprika
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Or パプリカ, which is Japanese for paprika but in Japan refers to the vegetable known in Canada as a red bell pepper.
Back to the paprika, it is a beautiful red colour, perfect for this time of year (December) as it fits in colour-wise with many other Christmas-y things.
One of my students gave me some paprika as a souvenir from travels in Europe and my first thought was of Goulash, a Hungarian dish featuring the use of paprika.
...The recipe I followed was simple and the results were delicious.
Served with rice and some vegetables, this made for a very satisfying meal, with enough leftovers for tomorrow for two of us.

item.title: It was chilly, so I put some chillies in my chili.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Living in Japan has shown me that Japanese can also have oddities in a language, and I'd assume the same is true for many, if not all languages.
...I put some chillies in the chili. Not too much, as my family doesn't like food to be too spicy.
I like to make chili the day before we eat it, so that the flavours can become deeper.
This morning I baked a pan of corn bread with jalapeños and cheese in it.

item.title: Naruto Moussaka
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I decided to use these sweet potatoes for making Moussaka, which in my opinion is a Greek-style lasagna made with the vegetables eggplant and potatoes instead of noodles.
But, before making the Moussaka, I had to make a pot of Chili which I'd promised to make for tomorrow's dinner (I like to make it a day ahead of time to let the flavours develop better).
After the Chili was cooking, I cooked the eggplant, first in the microwave, then baked in the oven to draw out moisture from the eggplant.
...Seeing as we'll eat the Chili tomorrow (with cornbread, of course) it looks like we'll eat the Moussaka on Monday.
...I know that each component, the sweet potatoes, the eggplant (rubbed with olive oil and salt and baked until golden brown), and white sauce taste great individually.

item.title: Red Pepper Jam
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
This is the second time I've made David Rocco's Red Pepper Jam, or as he named his recipe, Marmellata di Peperoncino di Gioia.
...I've always loved red peppers, in any form and this jam was great on cheese and crackers, on sandwiches, and with thin slices of dried meats/sausages.
I ran out of this jam sometime this year and when we picked up a few bags of red peppers on sale at the market recently, I knew I had to make this jam again.
...I don't have one anymore (I left it in Canada many years ago) and so I forced the peppers through a mesh screen. The pepper pulp is then cooked some more with sugar until it has a jam-like consistency.

item.title: Puppet Theatre & Sliding Screens /人形浄瑠璃と襖からくり
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
My wife and I drove just south of Tokushima city today to enjoy some traditional Japanese culture. ... In past times, local citizens would gather to enjoy some theatre after the harvests were finished in the fall.
...After several plays from the puppet theatre, the final show was a display of a multitude of background sliding screen changes.
There were many changes to the sliding screens, with the impression that the theatre was opening from the back going further and further back from the audience giving the perception of depth.
...This is one of only a few such outdoor theatres existing now in Japan, and the show of the screen changes is even rarer than the puppet theatre.

item.title: Pumpkin Pie
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I noticed once I came to Japan that I started to eat a lot more pumpkin in my diet in the form of Kabocha squash. I also noticed that I missed the smell, and taste of pumpkin pie in Japan because it is not part of the culture to eat it. Yes, you can find it at some bakeries or restaurants, but 99% of the time it did not taste like the pumpkin pie of my memories.
I first started making pumpkin pies in Japan, from scratch (ie. no canned pumpkin) and found that it was easy to make and delicious.
...Over the years, I've had online battles with idiots who claim to make pumpkin pie from scratch (ie. from the start, without anything pre-made) only to find that they use a can of pumpkin pie filling.

item.title: BBQ Sauce, a.k.a. Magic Sauce
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I love hot dogs of all kinds, but tonight we're having black pepper sausages in our hot dog buns.
One of the condiments we, as a family, like to use is BBQ sauce.
However, it is not usually possible to buy BBQ sauce where we live in Japan.
It is possible to get BBQ sauce, either by returning to your home country, having friends or family send the BBQ sauce to you, or by using an internet shopping site.
...I love Japanese food but when we eat non-Japanese food, it is often easier and tastier to make my own alternative to the food I cannot buy here.

item.title: 1 Potato, 2 Potato, Sweet Potato Pie
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
One of the ways I love to eat sweet potatoes is in sweet potato pie.
I had some free time today, it being Saturday, so I decided to make up some of this pie.
It takes a while to make it because I slowly bake the sweet potatoes so that they are fluffy soft yet sweet.
The sweet potatoes are forced through mesh to make sure the sweet potatoes have no lumps and can be smooth and fluffy in the pie.
...The first bite - you taste sweetness, spices, various layers of smells adding complexity, and it's gone.

item.title: Raised Garden Bed
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The cost of making it higher above the ground was too expensive at the time, so we made do with our design. Another unfortunate problem with the low level of the garden was that neighbourhood cats would visit and go to the toilet there, and our own dog, Muffin, would jump in and eat the vegetables.
...Recently the wood frame from the garden bed had been breaking apart due to water and insect damage and the time was coming for a new garden bed.
...After more thinking I came up with the idea I finally used. 2x4’s fit into the holes of the cement blocks, and these 2x4’s are all attached to a frame on top of the garden bed.
...After this first garden bed was finished, and seeing as I still had free time left in Silver week, I built two more garden beds.

item.title: Silver Week
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We’ve been celebrating Golden Week in Japan for as long as I’ve been here. It’s a nice long holiday stretch in the Spring, but because everyone has the holiday, travelling can be a busy, tiring event.
...Monday is Respect for the Aged Day and Wednesday is the Autumnal Equinox Day. Because Tuesday is between two national holidays, it has been granted holiday status.
...We have no major plans other than relaxing and enjoying the nice weather.

item.title: Shaving Cream, Revisited
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
If done daily, the cost of the shaving cream and razors, plus any extra creams bought for after shaving can add up to a lot of money per year.
Last year I wrote about going retro with my shaving habits by not using pre-made shaving cream, but instead using a shaving brush and shaving soap to make my own shaving cream.
...Looking into the prices of shaving cream, I’ve found that the cheapest shaving cream (excluding that which may be sold at the Dollar store, or in Japan, the ¥100 stores) seems to cost about ¥380 (about $3.80 CDN).
Given the cost of the shaving soap I use lasts about 10 months for about ¥2000 (about $20 CDN) and a can of shaving cream would last me about 2 months, I assert that the costs for both formats of shaving cream are almost equal.
...Having used shaving soap for years in Canada before coming to Japan I know that I enjoy using the shaving soap, it is easy to use, it isn’t expensive, my skin feels better, and it’s good for the environment.

item.title: Figs
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
When I was a child and I made my mother mad, a common response made by my mother during her rant would be the rhetorical question, ‘Do you know what you’re going to get?
...This word she used when she was mad was not understood by us, but due to the fact she was angry it must have meant something bad.
...Why did she tell us, when she was angry, that we would get figs???
She laughed and explained that her mother had said that to her and she didn’t understand it either, but if it worked for her mother (mind you, when her mother said it in Ukrainian, my mother understood the word, but she still didn’t understand why she’d get figs) it would work for her.
...It was a wee tree, yes, but this year for the first time it provided us with a handful of fruit, and for that we are grateful.

The bottom picture shows a dance performance performed by one of the 1st year classes.
I was also able to buy some snacks that were being sold, do some shopping at one of the many bazaars that were available, and to enjoy some singing and dancing from the students.

item.title: Yakiniku/Korean BBQ/焼き肉

However, while in Korea I could notice a difference in my health’s condition within a day or two because of the diet in Korea. I don’t really care why I felt good, but I’ll be happy with the fact that Korean food is healthy and delicious.
...The BBQ’ed meat was placed inside the leaf, then some kimchi was added, then a piece of garlic and then (sometimes) some Korean miso.
...One of the nice things about the Korean BBQ is that after eating, although you’ve filled you stomach it is not heavy. Everyone enjoyed the BBQ and was able to partake in some of the dessert for today, freshly made banana bread.

item.title: Apple Cinnamon Bundt Cake

Even in Japan I think it is not one of the major foods people eat. At home, it can be a little labour intensive if you want to have a large selection of foods, and at restaurants it can be expensive at times.

item.title: Grilled Pizza
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School

This was lifesaving because at that time I lived within a stone’s throw of several fast food restaurants that were constantly enticing me with their signs and the aromas from their shops.
...The pizza cooks much faster than in a regular oven so you must be well prepared and move quickly. ... Thus by the end of the evening, my daughters were confident enough to be able to grill their own pizzas, again and again.

item.title: O-bon/All Soul's Day/おぼん
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
People clean their houses and offer a variety of food such as vegetables, fruits and sweets to the spirits of ancestors in front of the butsudan (a Buddhist family altar) or a small spirit altar called a shoroydana.
...The graves are different from those in my country of Canada because many people in Japan are cremated, so the grave only contains some of their ashes and the complete body is not buried under a tombstone inside a coffin.
...While I found many people I knew in Canada withdraw from dealing with death and dying and often seem to think little of past ancestors, people in Japan through events such as O-bon think about death and dying as part of one’s usual life.
I’ve heard about Mexico’s Day of the Dead in recent years and think that it too, may be a healthy and positive way of dealing with death and dying.
...But I’ve found through my experience in Japan that O-bon is a healthy way to continue to think about and love those which we have lost.

item.title: Dancing Fools / 阿波躍り
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I was told that it’s a big dance festival in the city of Tokushima, where I was heading to.
Fast forward many years, and I now live in Naruto, a city that is a stone’s throw from Tokushima (I still think the cities should combine seeing as we here in Naruto have many positive things that would benefit a marriage of the two, but I digress...) and it’s another city with Awa odori.
Tokushima’s festival is 10 times as big as ours in Naruto, but if you don’t live in Tokushima the traffic, parking and movement around the city is slow during the festival.
...Awa odori for those that don’t know is a dance festival from long ago in this part of Japan where the locals decided to basically have a street party and the ruler at the time from this area let the people have their fun.
One of the things that makes Awa odori so different from other dances like this in Japan is that observers are invited to join in with the dancers.

item.title: We Are Officially Power Producers

It’s been a bit less than 2 weeks since we’ve had our solar panels installed, and yesterday the OK was given to flip the power switch to start the system.

item.title: Solar Panel Update

item.title: On They Go
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
As the rain continued, I wondered whether today’s plans would still be OK.

item.title: And So, It Starts.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Every time we had a company come to our house however, they would quickly tell us that the pitch of our house was too steep and that it would be impossible to do.
My research on the internet seemed to show that their arguments made no sense, but unless we were going to install solar panels by ourselves we’d resigned ourselves to believe that we’d never find a company in Japan to help us in our quest to use solar panels.
...Yes, it would cost money, but we think that if we are going to depend almost entirely (remember that we use a wood stove in the winter to heat our home) on electricity for our utility needs that the energy should NOT come from nuclear power.
I know that creating energy from nuclear sources can be extremely efficient, but it’s the problem of what to do with the various components after they have served their purpose.
...And so, today, with no rain, and no typhoon (this last one was slow, but fairly big) we could have a company come down and put up scaffolding around our house, in preparation for having the solar panels installed.

item.title: In Hot Water, But It's OK (EcoCute)
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Somehow the gas was connected to a heater inside the cabinet pictured and the water was re-directed back into the house, going back to the kitchen on the first floor and upstairs to the bath on the second floor.

item.title: IH Cooking
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
