...We didn’t plant any tomotoes, but we have a tomato plant growing.” and this continues with many of the plants we find in the garden.
Sometimes we think we are growing something good and tasty when after all that love, water, and attention turns out to be a nasty weed in disguise.
...The soil is dug up a few times during the year (when possible - if some surprise veges pop up, well then I can’t quite disturb them, now can I?)
...I planted a lot of different things this year but those shiso plants came up everywhere in the garden and I think choked out everything else.

item.title: Almost Ready
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I’ve done a bit of outdoor work over the last few weeks (oh, my aching back) and the picture you see above shows the fruits of my labours (or at least some of it).
...We don’t have really cold temperatures like I grew up with in Canada (not everywhere in Canada is really cold in winter), but with no central heating in the house, the wood stove is our main source of heat.
The amount of wood we have not might look like much to some of you, but it occupies a huge amount of our total yard space. Land is expensive in Japan and so we make do with the amount of land we were able to buy.
...Maybe in the future, I’ll be able to shrink the size of the wood until I need it thereby creating more space in my yard.

item.title: Going Retro
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Years and years ago, I got bored with the shaving creams available in stores and decided to try my hand at using a shaving brush to make my own lather.
...It becomes one of the simple luxuries of life to have warm shaving cream on your face, massaged onto your face by your own little brush.
...Well, I used Body Shop’s shaving soap for many years in Canada and had some with me when I came to Japan. But when I ran out of the soap, there was no Body Shop in my city to buy any more. It was a 2 hour, $100 trip to Osaka (that would include ferry ticket prices, train/subway station prices and any other costs) to buy more at the Body Shop there but that didn’t seem like a good investment of time and money.

item.title: Fig Newtons
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Over time, I’ve been thinking of Fig Newtons, probably because they’re made with figs and also because I can’t buy them here in Japan.
...The ingredients seemed clear enough and the pictures posted with the recipe helped me to figure out how to make them.
The cookie dough was easy to make but then it rests in a cold place for 2 hours. The cookie filling was easy to make, but takes about 2 hours to cook.
...In the end, I was rewarded with soft cookies with a sweet, fig-gy filling and both cookies and filling have a touch of orange zest that gives them a nice smell and taste.

item.title: Hammocks
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Recently, while I was sitting outside I realized that I miss relaxing in a hammock outdoors when the weather is nice.
This led to some internet searching, and eventually I found a hammock for a reasonable price. I thought about it for a few days and discussed it with my wife before eventually ordering it.
...We set up the hammock in the house for the first few days, and everyone, including Muffin enjoyed using it.
...I’m looking forward to many, many relaxing days spent using the hammock.

item.title: Tandoori Chicken
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Off we went to do the shopping, knowing we’d have to decide on tonight’s dinner menu.
...I marinated the chicken pieces in spices and yogurt all afternoon hoping that the rain clouds would be kind to us and not rain.
...The weather held out long enough for me to start the barbecue, and just start cooking the chicken before the rains came.
...The rains were off and on, but the rain was never too strong, so I could complete the chicken on the barbecue.
...Now that we’re finished, I give my permission for the skies to rain to their heart’s content.

item.title: In a Pickle
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
If you, the reader, do not like pickles, may I suggest that you kindly look at one of my other posts.
I grew up eating various pickles and was happy to learn that here in Japan there are lots of different pickles.
...I grew up eating many pickles that were often sour in taste.
...I generally make only 2 types of cucumber pickles, ones made only with salt in the water which ferment and naturally sour, and vinegar pickles that are placed in a salty vinegar brine and ready to eat with a day or two.
...Am I being wishy-washy by making and eating both instead of making and eating only one kind of dill pickle?

item.title: Muffin, Revisited
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The other morning, I happened upon Muffin having a doze in the morning while I was busy preparing for my lessons.
...Our family had a dog when I was a child, yet I never remember our dog sleeping on its back, feet in the air.
...Sometimes he’ll sleep on his side, other times on his stomach, and other times, as seen above, on his back.
...After breakfast, which includes some chopped apple after his regular food (don’t forget the apple!), he’s ready for a bit of play time before most everyone (sometimes including me) gets ready and leaves the house.
After a bit of play time (I can usually only afford a few minutes), he watches us, sometimes pouts, but begrudgingly acknowledges that we’ll be leaving him for a few hours.

item.title: 梅ジャム／Japanese Apricot Jam
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The Japanese Apricot or 梅(うめ）is used often to make pickled plums for eating with rice, or for steeping in strong alcohol and sugar to make a liqueur called Umeshu (梅酒).
I happen to be making some liqueur with Japanese Apricots right now, and recently I found a batch of pickled plums that I’d made a few years ago that weren’t so good after being made, but when tasted recently were found to be great.
...But yesterday I happened upon packages of Japanese Apricots for about 150 yen for about one kilogram of apricots (I didn’t bother reading the label or weighing them).
...I used no recipe but just cooked the apricots and copious amounts of sugar until it was thick and sweet-ish.
...The end result is a jam that is sweet yet sour, perfect with pancakes (which we had this morning) and also I think with meats in the future (with soy sauce, to make a sweet, sour, salty glaze).

item.title: Dumping on Dump Trucks
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I don’t know how dump trucks move in other parts of Japan, but where I live, they usually drive around in groups.
...Because when many of these trucks go down a road, they tend to go slower than regular traffic and they tend to go in multiple lanes.
...When these trucks move slowly, from behind you can see the dirty air being directed at any vehicles beside them on the right side.
I don’t know if it is better ecologically to have the exhaust pipes higher in the air, or in other places but I do know that if I happen to drive beside one of these vehicles, I must close my windows or suffer the wrath of breathing in dirty, smelly air.
...Might I suggest that if those pipes must come out on the right side, please point them downwards towards the road and not straight out at traffic.

item.title: Have You Tried the Razor Trick?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It seems if you slide your razor along your jeans (not while wearing them) in the opposite direction you would use for shaving, that you would sharpen the blades of the razor.
...I tried it out and found my razor was a little better than before I had sharpened it, but I was not completely convinced of the method.
While chatting with one of my brothers I mentioned the story about sharpening cheap razors and my brother told me about another method he’d read that mentioned using your arm to sharpen the razor.
...The only downfall was that the strip of material that is supposed to help lubricate the razor by providing aloe or some other chemical on your face ends up all over your arm while you sharpen the razor.
...I’m unsure how long I will be able to keep using the same razor, but for now, this method is saving me a lot of money and giving me a good shave.

item.title: A Berry Nice Way to Start the Day
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Sure, the fruit isn’t all perfect, but it’s from our yard, it’s healthy, and it tastes great.
It took a few years to finally get raspberries and blackberries growing on our property. In years past, the fruit would grow for one or two years at most and then die out. I planted these fruits in various places, but finally I’ve found places where they thrive.
...It will take a few more years to get them pruned properly, but it’s easier to cut them back than it is to get them growing.

item.title: Did Someone Say 'Perogies'?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I wanted the students to become familiar with this particular food, but little did I realize that I was actually hypnotizing myself to make more perogies.
...Combined with potatoes we received from a friend recently and we were well on our way to having all the ingredients for perogies.
I usually make potato and cheese filled perogies and sometimes include sauerkraut filled ones but rarely make my favorite dill and cottage cheese perogies due to the limitations of getting cottage cheese in Japan. Oh, I can buy it, but the containers usually contain little more than a few spoonfuls of cottage cheese.
...I made a lot more perogies today than I usually do, but I don’t worry as what we don’t eat today or tomorrow will be frozen and eaten in the near future.

item.title: Tacos Party
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Yet one of my earliest memories of eating something akin to Mexican food was eating flour tortillas at a restaurant when I was in Junior High School. At that time, we could have ordered the hard corn shell tacos, but we often ordered the wheat tortillas or ‘soft’ tacos, because they tasted just as good and they were less messy.
...Not all of our students choose to participate, but we always have students who enjoy coming to the party to enjoy making and eating tacos.
...The Tacos Party fits in with that idea, as it lets students enjoy food that is very rarely seen or eaten here in Japan.
...Most students were very open to experimenting with the different foods and I think most of them left with their bellies happy and full (others left being only happy).

item.title: Chimney cleaning
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I found that a cloth, re-useable bag is available that uses velcro to hold on to the pipe and which hangs down from the pipe, collecting the dust and soot.
...Next, I use the jack from my car to lift up one side of the stove, then the other and slide boards under the stove’s feet. Once on the boards, it is easier to slide my stove out of the way, so that I can feed the steel rods and brush up the pipes.
...The tape makes for a stronger entry area so that when I feed in the rods into the hole, the hole in the bag will not open up larger.
...I’m glad that it’s done, because now that the warm weather is upon us (with much warmer weather soon to come) I hate doing work wearing my dirty work clothes.

item.title: How I BBQ
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I should first note that this is the way that I BBQ and that what I am doing would not be considered BBQ-ing by some people. ... Cooking foods over fire is something basic and natural and I’m always happy to have the chance to cook outside.
I don’t like to use chemicals when I’m cooking, so I start my fire with wood shavings.
...Because I do a lot of wood chopping, I always have small pieces of wood that can be used to start my fire.
...For those of you in Japan who usually don’t BBQ at home, I encourage you to give it a try.

item.title: Sorrel Pesto
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
For example, you could serve it boiled, you could make it into a soup, you could use it in salads and sandwiches, or you could make it into a paste.
I’ve made all of the above, but I want to talk about sorrel pesto because I’ve just made some. Because sorrel is a bit sour already, you can use less lemon juice or vinegar when making your pesto.
...I mix the washed leaves with olive oil, salt and a touch of lemon juice or vinegar, adjusting the taste as I go.
...We froze most of this pesto and will continue to enjoy it through the summer and into the fall and winter, or whenever we finish it all.

item.title: In a bit of (a) Jam
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
We were lucky enough to be once again invited to go strawberry picking at a friend’s farm.
The weather, though a bit cloudy and hazy at the outset, stayed rain-free and was also quite warm.
...I made 3 batches of freezer jam, while my wife made an equivalent amount of cooked jam. We saved some strawberries for eating, and froze some of them as well.
Next weekend I look forward to making some pancakes and having them with our fresh jams.

item.title: 100 Yen Festival & Chair Race
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Not all products were 100 yen, as some were 200 or even 300 yen, but the concept was like the ubiquitous Dollar Stores (100 Yen Stores) in that many goods were just 100 yen.
...Though it is becoming increasingly rare, I still believe that streets like this one are important in cities.
...I think there used to be more and more of these all over Japan, but over time the dreaded shopping malls have killed them off.
...In its heyday, I believe the second storey of many of the buildings also housed shops, but not anymore.
...Mostly, we bought a variety of foodstuffs, but the festival also provided an opportunity to bump into friends and acquaintances.

item.title: April's Cooking Lesson
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The snake in today’s recipe was actually just meatloaf, shaped like a snake in the pan. The shape, as I said could be interesting for some (think small children who need prodding to get into the meal time fun) but another reason this shape is good is that it allows more of the meat to be browned, thereby increasing the flavour of the meatloaf.
...Finally, some onion gravy was made so that it could be eaten with the meat and pudding. ... We also had a simple salad of greens from our garden, and some tomatoes cut, and sprinkled with black truffle salt.
Dessert, for those who had room (everyone did), was a slice or two of some Blondies (no picture - oops!)

item.title: Cherry Blossoms
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It didn’t last all day, but it did last long enough for us to enjoy ourselves on a picnic.
We went to Naruto’ Sports Park because there are many cherry trees to enjoy and it also is large enough to offer a variety of locations for having a picnic with your choice of sun or shade.
...The cherry blossoms are filling in nicely but my guess is that later this week will probably be the best time to see them. ... At this time of year the weather is unpredictable with rainy, windy weather all to often putting an end to the cherry blossom viewing.
Now that the blossoms are here, we’ll be sure to enjoy them whenever and wherever we have a chance to see them.

item.title: Wild Canada
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Wild Canada is a CBC show about the importance of nature in Canada and the world.
The Wild Canada app is an e-book companion to this wonderful show.
This app features lots of nature information about Canada and includes lots of videos, sounds and pictures.
Canada’s history and nature is discussed/shown in this app and each chapter in the book is short yet full of lots of information.
Those of you who’ve been to Canada will be reminded of the beauty of Canada’s nature, and those of you who’ve yet to explore Canada will get a taste of what awaits you.

item.title: The 100-Year Old Man Who...
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The 100-Year Old Man Who Climbed out the Window and Disappeared is a great book!
...The cover design was nice, the cover picture relating to the title seemed simple, and the book design was different. Some pages of the book have a ragged edge to them which is not something I usually see.
...But the book also looks back at the 100-year old man’s life and what an interesting life he’s led!
I enjoyed this book very much because the writing was fun and interesting and it was a nice way to unwind at the end of the day (when I usually read).

item.title: March's Cooking Class
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
As I write this, I know there is still a couple of hours till dinner yet my tummy is happy.
...The chicken was prepared with various seasonings and cooked in the microwave. While it cooked, the picked vegetables were prepared, sauces were readied and other fillings were set up for the bread.
While the sandwiches were being filled, we also made a simple pho, a soup that included some noodles, herbs and seasonings.
...My thanks, as always to the wonderful company I enjoyed while cooking and eating.

item.title: Introducing: Clamato!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Both cocktails are similar in that the recipes can be altered to everyone’s individual taste, with more Tabasco for some, more black pepper for others, or more lemon or lime juice for yet others.
I have heard that Clamato is more popular in Canada than in the United States and now that I live in Japan I’d add that it isn’t popular here, as well. I hadn’t seen Clamato in my part of Japan for many years, but recently I’ve seen it at one or two specialty stores, available in small quantities for a fee.
...My younger brother sometimes drank a variation of the Red Eye, using the same ingredients for the Caesar but using beer instead of vodka. I’d seen him drink this mixture for years without the slightest interest in ever trying it, but a few years ago my curiosity got the better of my and after he made one of these drinks (he has no name for it) I asked him if I could taste it.

item.title: Otsukaresama / おつかれさま
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I first encountered the term when I came to Japan and was encouraged to say the term at the end of the day at the English school where I worked to the staff who still remained at the office, or to staff who were also leaving at the same time as myself. My understanding of the term was to mean that we had worked hard together that day, to acknowledge that fact, and to state that we were now finished and leaving the work situation to go home or elsewhere.
...Later in the day, finding that I had some free time and the weather was nice, I decided to tackle the job of breaking apart some of the bigger pieces of wood we have so they can fit in our wood stove.
...That one piece, now split into many small pieces can be used to heat our home for at least one day (we only need have a fire in the evenings now).
To the piece of wood now burning in my stove, we worked hard, you and I, today.

item.title: February's Cooking Class
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The chicken is quickly prepped and shoved in the oven while the dressing and greens are prepared.
Once the chicken comes out of the oven, the salad is dressed and the salad and chicken come to the table, where everyone helps themselves and mixes their own salad of greens, chicken and bread.
The meal is simple yet there are nuances that elevate this dish to more than the sum of its parts.
...A blossom of whipped cream, a spoonful of dark cherries, and a biscotti to enjoy with the chocolate pot.
...Yet any child, nay the child in all of us loved eating this down to the last spoonful, when we carefully cleaned the last remnants of chocolate.

item.title: Sad About Sochi
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Coming from Canada, where a lot of winter sports are part of many peoples’ lives the winter Olympics have always been more important for me than the summer games.
...In the past, I was able to see some of the Olympics because I had access to the national broadcaster in Japan (NHK) in the apartment where we once lived. It wasn’t the best possible solution for me, a Canadian in Japan as the broadcast focused on Japanese nationals, which is perfectly logical considering this is Japan.
...Our internet provider is also our TV channel provider and though we have a variety of Sports channels, none of them show the Olympics. The Canadian national broadcaster (the CBC) provides coverage for Canadians living in Canada via TV and an internet application, but this does not work outside of Canada.

item.title: The Best Laid Plans
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The story involves individuals involved with Canadian politics and a basic understanding of the Canadian political landscape might be required to fully enjoy this book.
Usually I try to read a few pages of a book before going to sleep at night. Some nights it can be difficult to get through 1-2 pages before I have to drift off to sleep. But with this book I had the problem of forcing myself to go to sleep after reading 10 or more pages.
...I will be checking on Amazon Books for the sequel to this book.

item.title: National Apple Pie Day!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
A quick Google search shows that May 13th is the National Pie Day in the United States.
However, as I live in Japan and seeing that there is no National Pie Day here, let it be proclaimed that today, January 5th, 2014 is hereby designated as National Pie Day.
...The pie was/is delicious (we haven’t finished it all yet) and this recipe will be a keeper. ... The apple filling stayed solid, not mushy and the flavour of the apples stayed strong rather than being over-powered by spices or the crust.
It’s nice going to bed knowing there’s apple pie for snacking on during the night, should one become peckish or awaiting one for delicious and quick breakfast (and healthy - it has apples in it!)

item.title: Christmas Dinner
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We’re a day late with our Christmas dinner this year, but it’s not a problem.
We enjoyed the roast chicken, mashed potatoes, gravy, stuffing, salad, pickles and olives as well as many cookies for dessert (along with some Canadian Ice Wine).
Simple and sweet. Good food, prepared at home with love. A family meal, enjoyed with each other’s company, talking, laughing, eating, enjoying.

item.title: The Case of the Missing Fruit
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
This year I thought I’d add dried cranberries because they taste great and they add a festive colour to the cookies.
...I’ve been buying the dried cranberries off and on all year at various 100 yen stores (the equivalent of a dollar store) in and around Naruto.
...Not only that, but merchandise has been moved around in many places so that you get the impression that they never sold the dried cranberries in the first place.
In the end, I gave up and purchased some freeze-dried strawberries thinking that their colour would be similar to that of the cranberries.
...I was almost finished with the cookie dough when I thought I should give one last check in our pantry in case there happened to be some remaining packages of dried cranberries.

item.title: 7 boxes of Christmas Decorations
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Well, it’s the end of November and I feel that now is the time to start decorating our house for Christmas.
I know some places like to start the Christmas decorations just after Halloween, but for me November isn’t the Christmas month.
...Over the years I’ve lived in Japan, my family has collected Christmas goods that we made, bought, were sent from overseas or we received from friends here in Japan.
Our items include 2 big Christmas trees, several wreaths, numerous lights, a huge assortment of ornaments, and a variety of other goods.
While I would like to show some of the decorated house to you, my main focus today was getting the boxes out and starting the decorating.

item.title: November's Cooking Lesson
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It is one of the first items I can remember learning to cook, and I took to frittatas quickly.
...It took a couple of tries to figure out what ingredients we wanted in today’s frittata but it wasn’t too difficult. We finally decided on leftover rice, asparagus, sausage and cheese to be thrown into the frittata. I’ve always made my frittatas with leftover pasta but we reasoned that more than likely, most people in Japan would probably have leftover rice more than leftover pasta.
...In the end, we decided to go with the brownie in a cup recipe that we’ve been using for a while and which our daughters love to use when they want a sweet snack.

item.title: Pickled Olives
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Well, if you will concede that coffee is a bitter product, I would say that on a 10 point scale that coffee would rate a number 2 while the humble olive would rate 8 or 9.
Over the years of pickling olives I have found no definite formula with regard to salt, water and olives. ... I try to think of the first olives that were accidentally cured by somehow landing in a puddle of sea water, and also how some brave soul decided to try those olives.
...Sure, they’re not the most beautiful looking olives out there but they more than make up for that with their personality.
I don’ know if this batch of olives will last us the whole year (until next year’s olive picking), but we’ll be sure to enjoy them until they run out.

item.title: Adventures in Olive Picking
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I didn’t bring my ladder with me but I thought I’ll just pick what I can reach and be satisfied with that.
...After a short time however, I was approached by a police officer and asked to show my special identification card (needed by foreigners in Japan) and then my driver’s license.
...A short time after this I was approached by a man (I’ll call him Citizen A) who asked some questions about my activities.
...I was surprised at the formality as in all my other experiences of olive picking I was always told to pick to my heart’s content because my efforts resulted in less olives dropping to the ground, thereby creating less mess to be cleaned up.
...But then another individual came by car, and hearing that the police had phoned the city and received permission started phoning for someone to bring a ladder for me.

item.title: 2013 Halloween Party
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Children, candy, games & activities: put these items together on a late October weekend and you’ll be discussing the annual Halloween party at our English school.
...Many years we’ve had cool, rainy days on the party day and though that weather better matches the theme of the party, it’s much easier to deal with this kind of party when the weather is nice.
...Many students enjoy their costumes so much that they end up voting for their own costume. In the end, 2 costumes came up with more votes than all others, and those two individuals were awarded prizes.
...I’m not sure what this skill will be useful for in the future, but during the party it makes the task of choosing a winner extremely difficult.

item.title: Olives from our garden.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I was surprised that the olives on our trees have managed to stay on the trees after all the typhoons we’ve had this year (the last typhoon which blew by last night was number 28 for the year).
...When the olives are green they can sometimes have not much pulp on them to eat. ... A blend of green and purple on the olives makes for good olives when I do the pickling.
...And when I think about it, a lot of recipes that I’ve used that call for olives usually ask for just a small handful of them.
I’m still going to try to get some more olives from other sources this fall, but these olives are the first to be picked and pickled this year.

item.title: October's Cooking Lesson
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Today’s menu was brunch-like, but was not labelled as such because I didn’t put many savoury items on the menu.
...We also had a bit of quiche that I cooked up last night and some fresh fruits.
With the savoury and sweet balanced on the menu, this menu had something for everyone. The sausages were great and the quiche was filling, which was surprising considering how small the piece was.
As for the waffles, I couldn’t decide which tasted better: the salted caramel sauce with whipped cream, the home-made strawberry jam (my wife’s) or the blueberry syrup made by the students.

item.title: September's Cooking Lesson
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It’s been a while since we had our last cooking lesson at our school, back in the spring of this year.
Today the students and I got back together for another round of cooking.
The recipes for today were Spicy Chickpeas with Ground Meat and a Pear Yogurt Cake.
...The carrot salad was a bit sour and a bit spicy due to the addition of some grated ginger.
...Of course, these pears taste best when eaten fresh, but there may be times when people have a lot of these pears at their home and would like to try them in another form.

item.title: I did it again.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I had bought a few new plants to grow during the winter (swiss chard, Italian parsley, arugula and a few others) and after the garden cleaning, carefully put them into their new home.
...It has a few plants in it, there are no weeds to be seen, and the soil texture looks good - neither dry nor wet, but something between.
...What’s strange is the method I tend to use which is to randomly throw seeds here and there without keeping any notes or putting in any markers with names, and hoping that everything will grow well.
...So, that’s why I’m warning you (and maybe myself, if I remember to look at this posting in a few months) about what may happen. Be ready to praise me if something nice grows and I crow about it, or to soothe my soul if I’m bitter about the poor state of the garden.

item.title: Good morning, summer!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I recommend you set your volume to maximum to get the true effect.
...Talking to individuals can be very difficult due to extraneous noise from cicadas.
...The little/big guys are only around for a short time so I can’t get too mad at them. They are also a summer sound, telling your brain, your body that it’s the warm part of the year and for this I’m thankful.
Still, if possible, could you guys/gals wake up a little later in the future.

item.title: I Relish Summertime
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I love them both and one of the condiments I like to use on them is relish. For hamburgers I can enjoy burgers with or without relish, but I really relish a hot dog with some relish on it. I guess part of my love of relish goes back to my childhood days, eating hot dogs with bright yellow mustard, bright red ketchup, and the bright green relish.
...It is possible to find at some stores, but it can be hit or miss and when you do find it, the portions tend to be very small.
...This small batch of relish should last me the year, seeing I’m the only one who eats it in my house (more for me, yay!).

item.title: What's for dinner? Naan of your business.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I picked up a package of Tandoori spice while in Canada last year and have been slowly using it for dinners. I marinated some chicken breast and drumlets in the spice mixed with yogurt, garlic and ginger all day and hoped for some nicer weather in the evening so I could cook the chicken over charcoal.
Thankfully, after heavy rains this afternoon the weather cleared and it looked like BBQ-ing would be OK. I figured since I’d have the fire going anyway, why not do some naan bread as well?
...It soon became a family affair with me on the BBQ, Mona rolling out the dough, and Emma brushing on the melted butter.
...After the naans were done, we grilled the chicken, cut it up and served it with mint and cilantro pestos made earlier in the summer.

item.title: Welcome, Summer.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I sat outside this afternoon enjoying the weather while sipping on some beer and Clamato.
The humidity is unbelievably high now so the components of the beer and Clamato helped me to keep my system ready to deal with the weather.
...Get out, touch nature, enjoy the weather while you can. Soon, too soon I’m afraid, the weather will start cooling off. Enjoy the heat, and help to make things easier by eating and drinking refreshing foods and drinks.

item.title: At the Sunday Market in Kochi
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
While I’ve been to Kochi prefecture a few times, due to my wife’s hometown of Mugi being close to Kochi prefecture, I’ve never been to Kochi city.
...However I noticed that if you don’t like tunnels, then this would be a difficult drive (ie. lots and lots of long tunnels).
We had a good time looking at the wares at the various stalls and bought a variety of items along the way. Our lunch was a collection of foods, some from the stalls in the market and some from the huge food court near the end of the market place.
...A volunteer guide gave us an English tour of the castle, providing us with many fun facts as well as information about Kochi.

item.title: Happy Dad's Day
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It was quite a busy day at the pool, but I’m always happy to play around in the pool.
Dinner was a smoked, bbq’d chicken that quite a treat, as we rarely eat a whole chicken, never mind one that is bbq’d. I did the cooking but it was actually easier than cooking smaller pieces as there was less work to do. There are no pictures to show but hey, it was a choice of eating or taking a picture and then eating and really, you’ve probably seen bbq’d chicken before.
...We (father’s) are often not as celebrated as are the mothers but we love and are loved just the same.

item.title: An Atypical Lunch in Japan
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
There have been some changes over the years, as we’ve altered the menu items here and there and played around with the party activities.
...We do some activities at the start of the party, then go into the kitchen, wash up and then get into making tacos.
...Part of the reason may be that there seem to be less and less students studying, and another reason may be that the party is pretty much the same from year to year and therefore may be boring to some individuals.
...The children have a chance to make and eat a food that is not common in Japan, which is another unique opportunity. Finally, the children have a chance to cook and eat in someone else’s house, other than their own.

item.title: On the menu: Quiche
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Lately we’ve received onions from a few different people who’ve grown them and shared them with friends. We had lots and lots of onions, so last night I decided to cook some of them and save them for the future. That way, when we need cooked onions, I can just pull them out of the freezer, plop them in the pan and away we go.
After chopping the onions (I’m guessing about 4-5 litres or so) I cooked them down according to this recipe.
It took a long time to cook down because the onions were fresh and had a lot of water.

item.title: Leaf it to me.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Since we have a lot of shiso, mint and cilantro growing in the garden we decided to use some of it to make pesto.
The basic recipe we use is the same for each ingredient, though sometimes small changes are made when making a certain type of pesto. We like to use fresh leaves of some sort, garlic, cashew nuts, parmesan cheese, olive oil, lemon juice, salt and a touch of vinegar.
...Now that our children like pesto, these three batches of pesto will probably not last long. No worries, as by the time they are gone we’ll have more leaves available for making more pesto.

item.title: …and you shall receive.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
When we have more than enough of something, we try to share with neighbours and friends.
...It began with a student bringing a bag of red onions harvested from the garden.
Later, a neighbour gave two bags, one with white onions and carrots and another with potatoes, all from the garden.
...In Japan, people are thankful for the food they eat and say “いただきます/ i ta da ki ma su” to say they are thankful.
After eating, people say “ごちそうさまでした/ go chi so sa ma de shi ta” to say thank you for your treat (of food).

item.title: Taking the ferry to work.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The university is a 15 minute car ride from my house, and roughly the same amount of time is needed to go by bicycle.
...Naruto University of Education is located on Takashima Island which is accessed either by one of two bridges from Naruto city or by ferry.
...It takes me less that 10 minutes to cycle to the ferry dock from my house.
...If you look closely, the boat is on the other side of the channel straight in front of the pier.
...If you ever visit Naruto, remember to take a free ferry ride to Takashima.

item.title: May Flowers
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
This is the flower arrangement my daughter made this week in her flower arrangement class.
The theme was ‘May Flowers’ and compared to the April arrangement, which was soft and quiet with the cherry blossoms, this arrangement shouts out its colours and stands like a peacock announcing that it’s spring.
With the nice, warm weather we have now and no more cool or cold weather, I whole-heartedly agree.

item.title: Strawberry Pie
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
A simple pie crust is on the bottom.
Next, a layer of custard covers the bottom of the pie.
On top of that, fresh strawberries were sliced then mixed with freshly made freezer jam and placed on top of the custard.
Whole strawberries cover the top of the pie.
Finally the top of the pie is covered with a jelly glaze.

item.title: When the world gives you strawberries...
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
This was my first view down the first row of the strawberry hot house I was in today.
We’ve been lucky enough to be invited many times to the strawberry farm of friends of ours for many years now.
...By this time in the strawberry farm work schedule we’ve been told that these hot houses have reached the end of their main production. Soon the plants will be tilled into the ground and new plants will be planted and the cycle will begin anew.
...This year, I took a quick wander down a second and then third row (each house contains 6 rows) to sample strawberries in those places.

item.title: Happy Mother's Day 2013
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Happy Mother’s Day to all mothers.
In memory of my mother, I baked a raisin pie for our Mother’s Day dinner.
The pie is simple to make and simple in taste but it is comfort food.
Mothers provide comfort, as mine did and now my wife does for our children.
A simple present in honour of mothers was enjoyed by all after dinner.

item.title: Golden Week Holidays
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The week of holidays that occur at the end of April and beginning of May are called the Golden Week holidays.
This year the weather was great for most of the holiday period.
...During the holidays we went shopping at Youme Town (a shopping mall), went to an onsen (hot spring), went to Mugi for a couple of days, went to the beach, went swimming, and put new sod in our backyard. Add in a birthday, a wedding anniversary and (coming soon) Mother’s day and it really is a golden week.
It was a nice holiday break, but with all the work done yesterday, I’m looking forward to going back to work!

item.title: Hole-y Cow.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
What caught my eye is the strange number of holes drilled into the concrete support column.
There appears to be no pattern to the holes and on each column the pattern of holes is different. I don’t know if this is random drillings or some set plan for the holes, but it makes no sense to me.
...But if that’s the case, why weren’t they made stronger to begin with? ... If there was an earthquake, would the holes currently in the columns weaken the column?

item.title: Simple BBQ-ing
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
At the park we could occasionally smell some of the BBQ’s going, so on our return journey home we picked up some hot dogs for the BBQ.
Yesterday at a market we found some zucchini and that became the first course to grill today.
Because we were only cooking a little bit of food I decided not to use our BBQ but instead use a simple aluminum tray.
...I finished the zucchini by adding the grilled zucchini to a metal tray that contained some olive oil, balsamic vinegar, garlic and salt and pepper. Covered with foil and placed on the grill for a few minutes, the flavours mixed and the zucchini was coated with a nice sauce.

item.title: Have you tasted Konatsu?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The Konatsu fruit looks like a round lemon and the rind, when cut or squeezed to release the oils smells a bit like a grapefruit (not as strong) and a bit like grass. ... If this is what heaven smells like, I’ll be mighty pleased if and when I get there.
...The cut fruit again resembles a lemon, but it is a bit softer than a lemon.
...A big difference between Konatsu and other citrus fruits is in the pith that surrounds the juicy fruit.
...Remember not to take off all of the white pith and you will be rewarded with a most delicious fruit.

item.title: Update: Robot Vacuum
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Well, we’ve been using the new robot vacuum every day since we bought it and it’s time to give an update about its value.
My wife and I have noticed that when we use our traditional bag-less vacuum, we always get a large handful of dog hair in the vacuum.
...We are guessing that the hair in the robot vacuum is compressed into a small area, whereas the traditional vacuum leaves the hair in a larger, expanded state.
...We have found it best to remove as many obstacles from the floor as possible before vacuuming, including lifting dining chairs onto our table. This may not be possible or convenient for some people, but it save a lot of battery power that would otherwise be used banging to and fro inside and between the chair legs.

item.title: Another addition to the family.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Our other recent addition to the family, Muffin (see here and here) seems to shed some hair from time to time.
...Due to all the extra floor cleaning, we started thinking about getting a robotic vacuum cleaner but have held off because they are always so expensive.
This changed recently when we found out that a local home goods store, Nitori (ニトリ) also started selling this product, but for a lot less money.
Finally this weekend my wife and I had some free time and thus we went to check out the vacuums for ourselves.
...It will not be the primary vacuum in our home, but will (hopefully) help dealing with Muffin.

item.title: Tulips
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I took my daughter and some of her friends to a swimming pool today, and across the street this is what we saw.
Every year this area grows lots and lots of tulips and loads of people come to see and enjoy.
The tulips are in full bloom now and will not last much longer. If you have a chance you should see the tulips, located in Kitajima.
The beautiful colours of the tulips are another sign that spring is here.

item.title: A Weekend Wrap-up
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
To this, I add the work done here at our English School which involves a lot of class juggling in the spring. Some students leave due to school demands, others join, others must change the day or time due some other commitment, whether sports, music or cram schools.
...We’d planned to get together with friends last weekend on Sunday to have a picnic and enjoy the last of the cherry blossoms, but Saturday we received buckets of rain and typhoon-level winds.
...We happily were able to get together with our old neighbours on Sunday afternoon at our house for a short visit.
...Sunday also saw me finally fit a wire grid into our tool shed to hang tools on, pick weeds, and trim bushes.

item.title: Egg-cellent!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes we’d have them for breakfast, sometimes they’d be used for lunch to make egg salad sandwiches, sometimes they’d be snacks as devilled eggs, and sometimes they’d be pickled in vinegar and spices.
...Seeing as I had already thawed minced meat for our dinner, this sounded like a good opportunity to make Scotch Eggs for the first time in my life.
...After they eggs were peeled, they were wrapped in seasoned minced meat, floured, dipped in egg (another egg!), then in breadcrumbs and fried in oil.
...My daughters told me that they sometimes get this food as their school lunches, prepared at school by the school dieticians.
...I had to leave to teach some lessons just after I finished cooking these, so I couldn’t see if my daughters would eat them or not.

item.title: Happy Spring
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The picture above shows some cherry blossoms that I found this weekend while I was visiting Mugi.
...I’m surprised by how quickly the blossoms came out, seeing as that on Friday morning there were still few blossoms to be seen.
...Over the next week we will continue to enjoy the blossoms’ beauty and if they last long enough, we may still have a chance to picnic under the blossoms.
...As we were not going to be home for Easter Sunday, our girls did some Easter egg decorating on Friday morning, and then did some quick chocolate Easter egg hunting on Saturday before we left for Mugi. With Muffin being around this year, all the eggs had to be found before he came out of his crate, lest he find and consume the egg/chocolate.

item.title: Universal Studios Japan
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
USJ (Universal Studios Japan) has been near to us for quite a long time now, but up until this weekend, we’d never made the pilgrimage there.
We’d been to Tokyo Disneyland and Disney Sea and had a good time there, but a visit to the Magic Kingdom means a plane ride and usually at least one night’s stay in a hotel.
...We walked 5 minutes to catch a tour bus that stopped in front of the Naruto train station and in just under 2 hours, we were at USJ.
...Also, the number of visitors was expected to be very high due to all kids being on Spring vacation now, but the wait times for the most part were tolerable.
We enjoyed many rides and attractions while there and even though we didn’t see everything we a lot.

item.title: White Day Treats
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
White Day is quickly approaching, so I decided to make some treats to give to those who gave me sweets in February for St.
...I often make marshmallows (see this entry) but decided to try something new this year.
...They are like bite-sized pieces of Mounds Chocolate Bars.
...Coconut Chocolate Bites were so easy to make and they taste so great that I’m going to add them to my list of treats to make at Christmas.
Now it’s time to clean up the kitchen and you know, that isn’t so bad when you get to nibble on little bits of coconut and chocolate.

item.title: Jenga, anyone?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
What I do after chopping wood is similar to Jenga with a difference: I don’t want the stack of wood to come down!
...I really appreciated the help because bending down to pick up the wood over and over gives me a lot of back pain.
...I liken wood stacking to a puzzle, in that each space can be filled with the proper size and shape of wood.
...Years ago I cut and stacked wood in Mugi, then after it had dried sufficiently I brought it back to Naruto.
...Considering that I don’t have a lot of space in my yard it’s important to use the space as efficiently as possible.

item.title: Chocolates and Flowers
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
My daughter’s recent flower arrangement class tackled the theme of Valentine’s by combining 2 popular items from that celebration, namely flowers and chocolates.
My daughter’s creation includes only a couple of real chocolates (they’re inside the glass, resting on a bed of fake chocolate) but the colours and items used look pretty real.
I think my daughter did a great job choosing her colours and doing all the arranging.
Happy thoughts of love to you!

item.title: At the beach in Hawaii - NOT!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Another option is to cut wood on your property, if you have a lot of trees growing on your property. My friend in Canada does that because he has lots of trees, it helps keep the forest thinned properly and it’s convenient for getting the wood.
...Also, heavy wood burns nice but it’s not good in early fall or late spring because it burns so hot. In early fall/late spring we need a fire to get rid of the chill and not burn for hours, so a lighter wood is better.
...If I can get 2 or 3 more loads like this, I’ll be good for next winter and I won’t have to think about it all summer.

item.title: Muffin's 1st Visit to a Dog Park
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We’d heard of some different dog parks and cafes in the area so we decided to visit one today.
...We found information about the place here, but you could also visit the homepage for Dog Freaks MONICA.
...He still hasn’t had any real contact with other dogs because whenever he encounters other dogs, he is too excited and this makes other dogs nervous. Still it was good for him to come into contact with other dogs, and the owners of the other dogs at the cafe today were very kind towards us and Muffin and we appreciate their interactions with us.
We enjoyed drinks at the cafe (Strawberry Milkshake, Chai Latte, and Almond Latte) and next time may order some of the food as well as it looked yummy.

item.title: I had a craving for bagels today.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
We can now (after living many, many years) buy bagels at some bakeries and even some frozen bagels at the odd shop. But the shops that bake them are not so close and the frozen ones are not as good as freshly baked.
...I had tests to mark, lessons to plan and teach, the dog to walk and so on.
...Next time (maybe in a few weeks), I’ll smoke some salmon with some of that cherry wood I recently picked up. Bagels with the salmon and some cream cheese will be a great breakfast/snack/lunch/dinner.

item.title: February's Cooking Lesson
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The chicken adobe was tangy, and with the addition of coconut milk very rich tasting. ... Steamed white rice was good for enjoying every last bit of the adobo sauce.
...The cake is custardy on the bottom and slightly crunchy on the top. Loaded with apples it was a great finish to the meal along with coffee and tea.
As always, thanks to the students for the great job and great time.

item.title: An Honest Day's Work
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Do you ever have one of those days where you cut wood with a chainsaw for a couple of hours, then load over 500 kg of wood into and out of your car?
...Our current supply of wood for this year is quickly dwindling down but with some luck we should have enough to heat our house for the rest of the winter.
...In those days, every winter there would be a few days with a bit of snow on the ground - not enough for shovelling mind you, but enough to get your feet cold and wet.
...I found a few nuggets of wood that are sufficiently dry enough to burn now, so I not only have more wood for next year but for about a week of this year as well. Speaking of which, now that I’m cleaned up and this is finished I should get on with starting a fire and warming the house.

item.title: Chris Hadfield
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
My brothers had more smarts as to what was happening, but that didn’t stop me from doing a science project on rockets in elementary school.
...When I was about 11 years old, my family went on a vacation to Florida, US, and one of the stops we made was at NASA. It was at NASA that we first heard (and watched, as a movie) about the new Space Shuttle program that would carry people out to space as a rocket and then fly back home to Earth as an airplane.
...With the recent addition of Chris Hadfield as the commander of the International Space Station (ISS), my interest in space has once more been re-awakened.
I’ve been following Commander Hadfield on Twittter (@Cmdr_Hadfield) and enjoying not only the day to day reports of what’s happening, but the pictures as well.

item.title: An Ode to the humble Cabbage Roll
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
that cabbage rolls with meat are not the norm,
I know for fact, from my his-to-ry
that cabbage rolls should be meat-free!
...A Christmas package with that which can't be bought:
...Into each leaf it's rice that I stuff,

item.title: January's Cooking Lesson
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Today’s menu: Beef Hash, Jacket Potatoes, Tomato Smokey Beans, and Salad with Avocado Dressing.
...The beef hash has beef in it, of course, but it also contains a lot of sliced vegetables. The jacket potatoes were microwaved, then baked so that the outside was crispy but the inside was soft and fluffy. The beans were cooked with tomatoes and bacon and end up having a lot of umami. The salad was simple lettuce, arugula and avocado with a green goddess-like dressing made from avocado.

item.title: Cooking Lesson's Xmas Party
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Every year, since my first year of offering cooking lessons (close to 10 years now!) I have not taught a lesson in December, but instead had a Christmas party with my students.
This years party was a simple affair and the menu included vegetable soup, freshly baked bread, deep-fried fish served with vegetables in a vinaigrette, roasted chicken, mashed potatoes, gravy, and for dessert cinnamon apple cupcakes with frosting and sprinkles.
The food was great but more than the food I found happiness in the conversation and company. And this, to me is one of the things the holiday of Christmas is about, spending time with people you love and having the connection with each other.

item.title: Muffin Dog
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Our little guy had some surgery this weekend (neutered) and he’s back with us now.
...Muffin can be seen from time to time snoozing in his bed or on a carpet, but he’s also pretty good at shadowing us.
...Generally Muffin is well-behaved and quiet which is good because we have our school in our house and a noisy pet would be troublesome. He does like to play with sticks and as we have a wood stove he can often be seen sneaking a branch out of the wood box, either to practice his biting skills or to get our attention (in such cases he’ll wander in front of us with the branch sticking out of his mouth like a fat cigar, checking to see whether or not we’ll chase him).
This year will be Muffin’s first Christmas with us, and if he continues to be a good boy, he may just get something special in his stocking (No, he doesn’t have a stocking yet, but my daughters have mentioned the idea many times so he may just end up with one).

item.title: November's Cooking Lesson
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
One of the themes for today’s cooking lesson was to make use of common items that are found in most homes. ... Recently both of my daughters came home from school with a daikon radish that they had received (as did all the other children) from the school.
...The daikon gratin is a rich dish, made with some cream and cheese and so to balance out the meal we needed something lighter and something that would help to cut the richness in the mouth. ... When mixed and eaten together, the citrus provides a nice kick after all the cream and cheese from the gratin, but the spicy squid, mint and fish sauce keep the dish from being just tart tasting.
...Using store bought tarts (another theme in this lesson was to make things easy, so the meal could be made in a short time) students mixed just a few ingredients to create the cranberry filling.

item.title: Membrillo (Quince Paste)
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I usually can find quince (in Japanese カリン or 花梨) at markets or parks, but this year I hadn’t seen any and felt forced, yes forced to buy some at the supermarket.
If you’ve never seen quince, they are yellow or green (not ripe) and look like pears with the small end pushed in.
...I’ve made jelly in past years but last year I made membrillo and decided this year to make some more because I enjoyed it so much.
...I’ve read that membrillo is good with cheese and I agree that it’s good with a salty cheese.
...So, if you happen to see some quince in the stores, or better yet in your neighbour’s garden (ask your neighbour before taking it) get some and try making some membrillo .

item.title: A Happy Food and Drink Day
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
After a morning walk with Muffin and some breakfast, it was off to the matsu ura shu zo sake factory for their annual open house festival.
...It may have something to do with the various shots of sake and shochu I had before the tasting contest or (could it be?)
...After a wonderful time at the festival, I returned home and then attended the B級ご当地グルメフェスティバル (B Level Gourmet Food Festival) in Tokushima.
...In the middle on the left is a sandwich filled with fried shitake mushrooms and bacon, and on the right there is barbequed chicken (that was supposed to be served with over rice with a special sauce, but the rice wasn’t ready and we were told me would have to wait from 5-10 minutes, so we passed; next time it would be better if they are better prepared).
...B Level Gourmet Foods have really become famous in Japan because they are simple but delicious foods that are found all over the country.

item.title: 2012 Halloween Party
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We had close to 30 students this year participate in our school’s annual Halloween Party.
Our party is one hour long, but has many events, including best costumes and a mummy-making event.
Due to privacy concerns, I can’t show many of the pictures from the event. Those pictures will be available to families of the students.
Suffice it to say fun and candies were had by all (by all!)

item.title: Movie Day
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The movie for those that don’t know this a true story about women from Tokushima (the area in Japan where I live) who started a business selling leaves. ... It is a beautiful area in Japan, but the population in the area keeps dropping and families can find it difficult to make their living.
The movie shows how individuals came up with the idea of selling various leaves from the local country side that could be used in restaurants all over Japan to decorate food dishes, as seen in this site. What’s amazing about this story is that the people who run this highly successful business are all older women.
...The movie’s story was simple, beautiful and one can’t help but stop and think about the simplicity, yet beauty of something as simple as leaves.

item.title: October 2012 Cooking Lesson
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
The last time my students and I had a cooking lesson was at the end of winter this year.
...The meal included a Thai curry soup, a Thai salad, and lemongrass bars for dessert.
...Many people have it growing in their gardens as it fills in spaces nicely and has a pleasant scent when touched. But lemongrass has a lemony quality different than citrus fruits, such as lemons or sudachis.
The students did a great job preparing all foods and it was wonderful to get together with them.

item.title: Really, Air Canada?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I applied for a bereavement rate here in Japan before returning to Canada, only to be told it was not possible. In Canada I was told it was possible, but it would seem from the difficultly staff had in finding forms and then going through the application process that this is not something that is done very often in their daily routines.
...After many weeks, I received an answer from Air Canada informing me that my outrageously high fare was not eligible for the bereavement rate.
But according to the letter (this information is not on the web page), the bereavement rate is not possible within Canada, to or from the U.S., to or from Hong Kong, from Japan to Canada, or in Executive Class.
...Peculiar thing about the Japan-Canada link; if my parents and I switched places, and my parents died in Japan while I lived in Canada, I could then fly out to them and receive the bereavement rate.
