item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School

item.title: Sports Day at School
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
My daughters had their annual Sports Day at school today and while the event was exciting, the weather was also a major event.
...When we later came to the school we found the centre of the school ground damp, but perfectly fine for the day’s events.
...There are activities for the very young, who are often attending with parents watching the older siblings as well as activities for the elderly, who likewise have come to watch grandchildren.
...The day’s event continually pit red against white and at the end of the day, points are tallied and one of the two colours wins.
...It seems the school ground was REALLY wet when the children first arrived, and so children and teachers used rags to mop up as much moisture as possible, squeezing the water into buckets which were then emptied away from the school sports ground.

item.title: Lemon-Sudachi Meringue Pie
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
The other night, while reading the book ‘Amelia Bedilia’ with my daughters, my younger daughter said ‘Dad, let’s bake some pies.’
...I needed a half cup of juice for my pie recipe and sudachis had a lot of seeds, making squeezing them a chore.
I double-checked with my daughter who allowed me to use both sudachis and lemons to make the pie.
...I also added the zest from both the lemons and some of the sudachis, so the little dark specks in the pie picture above are pieces of sudachi zest.
...Considering that I still have a lot of sudachis in the fridge, I think I’ll be making some more pies in the next couple of days.

item.title: Shiso Pesto
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
As summer has wound down and the vegetable garden has emptied it’s wares, we still have a lot of basil and shiso growing. We continue to add both of these herbs to our cooking, our salads and even our sandwiches.
But we like to preserve some of their flavour for the future by making pesto.
...Other pestos we make tend to have cheese and other items to round out and complement the herbs flavour, but we prefer our shiso pesto with little more than the oil, acid and some nuts to add a bit of richness.
We eat this pesto with various noodle dishes, both Japanese and Italian, on pizza and bread, and even in salads.

item.title: Pickled Peppers
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I didn’t think too much about it but I knew that between my wife and myself we’d find a use for the peppers soon. Last night I happened to catch a bit of one of Jamie Oliver’s TV cooking shows where he was making pickles.
...Once grown up I’ve come think that there are pickle people and non-pickle people, and to the people in the latter group, sorry, but you’re missing out on one of the simplest treasures in the food world. One of the first recipes I had to nail down (through telephone calls, mail, and e-mail) once I’d moved to Japan was my mother’s recipes for cucumber pickles.
...Back to the Jamie Oliver cooking show, what caught me off-hand was his use of oil for the pickling medium.

item.title: Summer Flower Arrangement
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
My oldest daughter recently started studying flower arrangement as a hobby.
Yesterday she had a lesson and the theme was about summer.
...Included in the arrangement are a number of different flowers (I have no idea of the names) and a smattering of sea shells. The bottom of the container is wrapped in two different blue coloured crepe paper giving (in my un-educated guess) the illusion of the sea.
I think my daughter’s creation is beautiful and I’m pleased as punch to have it for show in my classroom.

item.title: Chocolate Banana Ice Cream
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
The ice cream is banana flavoured and it is covered with chocolate. The name chocolate banana ice cream is a good name for this product.
...The chocolate is a little bitter making it a good match for the sweet ice cream (but not too sweet).
...These taste great and in this weather (it’s hot!), they go down pretty good.
...Pick these up if you can and eat them quickly because….. it’s hot!

item.title: Pizza Sunday
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
The pizza crust is whole wheat with added wheat bran, making the base pretty healthy.
The girls’ pizza was pepperoni and bacon.
...The adult pizza had shrimp (from the night before), olives, green peppers, onions, and shimeji mushrooms.
In all, we had three pizzas: the pepperoni/bacon, the adult mixed, and a third which was half and half (half for the girls and half for the adults).
Everyone’s tummy felt good afterwards and there was even a little space for some ice cream.

item.title: I'm Going to a Garden Party
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It’s summer, it’s the weekend so we of course had a BBQ.
We had friends over for the evening and with all the food that was available it was quite the feast.
We had a small beef roast that was BBQ’ed and lightly smoked with cherry wood (served with 3 sauces). We had BBQ’ed unagi (eel), grilled, coated with a teriyaki sauce, then re-grilled. Courtesy of a student, the unagi was delicious: smokey, sweet, salty, tender and yummy.

item.title: A Busy Afternoon in the Kitchen
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
The adult’s quiche had garlic fried spinach, balsamic vinegar fried onions, a small bit of cheese and some lemon sage.
...Then, while the quiches baked, I used the leftover potatoes from yesterday’s perogies (those are nearly all gone) to make another batch of perogies. My original intention was to freeze these perogies for a later date to be used as a snack or meal. However, certain little people in the house vetoed my plan and therefore the perogies will be consumed within the next day or two.
I was out of the kitchen by 5 PM and was able to relax for a full hour before dinner.

item.title: Perogies
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
In recent weeks, we’ve been lucky enough to get potatoes from friends and acquaintances that they grew in their gardens.
We’ve been enjoying them a number of ways (boiled, with some olive oil, herbs, salt and pepper), fried (hashed browns) and so on.
...My daughters also love perogies, so tonight’s dinner was popular with them.
My youngest daughter helped making the perogies, from the dough, to the potato filling, to filling and shaping the perogies.
...We had a good feast of perogies tonight and while there were a few leftovers, I don’t expect them to last too long.

item.title: A new addition
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
We picked up Muffin earlier today, and because of his off and on napping, we’re still getting to know him.
...Muffin is a Pug and his size and personality should mesh pretty well with our family’s lifestyle.
We’ve been reading books, watching TV shows, buying all sorts of items, and adjusting our home to help him fit in.
...Muffin is currently sleeping and he and I are the only two home right now.
...On behalf of Muffin let me please say that it’s nice to meet you all and here’s to a good relationship with you all.

item.title: Onion Bread
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
The bread is still cooling so I can’t say what it tastes like but it does smell great. Along with the caramelized onions I added some of my, yes, my olives that I pickled last fall.
...But that’s OK because if I want to eat any of those spreads there is other bread in the house to use. No, this bread will be good as is, or toasted, or in a sandwich, or with a plate of balsamic vinegar, olive oil, salt and pepper.
...The house smells wonderful, even though I had to have the oven going on this muggy day to bake up this bread.

item.title: Caramelized Onion Dip
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Since I will be making some no-knead sourdough bread this weekend I thought the addition of some onions would be a nice change from regular sourdough.
...And since I made more than enough onions for my bread recipe, I decided to use half of the onions for onion dip.
...Kenji López-Alt’s recipe for onion dip (see recipe here) and had a taste I was astounded!
I grew up as a kid having dried french onion soup powder mixed with sour cream (and a few other additions mixed in) to use as a dip with potato chips. ... Here in Japan it’s difficult to find dried onion soup powder, and scoff if you will but I find that the soup powder mixed with yogurt or sour cream or other foods gives a big dose of umami.

item.title: Lotus Roots
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
If you’ve never had lotus roots, there is a good chance you’d like them. The outer part of the root must be peeled off, and then the root should be rinsed. ... Often there is a little bit of the soil on the outside of the root, as well as inside.
...We often eat lotus root that has been thinly sliced, then fried with some soy sauce, saké, and sugar. ... Tempura is also another way we enjoy it, as well as just fried like potato chips.

item.title: Bar - be - Q
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
If you left a big, juicy steak in front of a lion and said, “Please wait a moment while I get my camera and take a picture.”
...Tonight’s BBQ included shrimp with a garlic, sudachi (like limes; sudachi are native to this area of Japan), olive oil sauce, chicken breast with the same sauce, chicken wings with 2 sauces: Alabama BBQ chicken sauce, and Montreal Steak spiced BBQ sauce.
We also ate baked potatoes courtesy of our neighbours next door who dug up their potatoes this morning and were kind enough to share with us.
...The 2 BBQ sauced foods went back on for another minute or two to caramelize and further flavour the chicken.
Though I love beef for BBQ’s, when you have a meal turn out like it did tonight you really are thankful for the BBQ’s ability to create so many different delicious foods.

item.title: I see(d) you.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I continued to try and grow grass, putting more sod, lots of grass seed and various items to keep the cats out. ... Eventually I decided to put a test plot on one area to see if anything would grow as there is a lot of shade on this side of the house.
...Recently, a good friend of ours, the carpenter who built our house moved back to Canada (you’re missed, but good luck with everything back in Canada).
...Until I plant more raspberries, I decided to go crazy with some of the various seeds we have.
...She may be right, but I prefer playing, having fun and maybe, just maybe growing something on this little piece of land that until recently had nothing but a little grass, cat do-dos, and weeds.

item.title: 2012 Annual Tacos Party
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Nevertheless, the food is not usually eaten by most families in our city and I would venture, in Japan as a whole.
...All students did a great job, but those students who’ve come to one or more parties are experts at making the tortillas. ... They were busy rolling out tortilla after tortilla and bringing them for us to cook up in the kitchen. Each student was asked to make from 2-3 tortillas, but some of the faster students did 6 or more!
...A big thank you to my family for all the work they did, as well as all the students and their families for their participation in this event.

item.title: Gyoza
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Recently my eldest daughter has been reading, or should I say devouring a book from the school library on gyoza.
...The benefit of this latest book, apart from the knowledge she gained and in turn, taught to us was the end result of our dinner tonight.
My daughter has done all kinds of cooking as she’s grown up though this was her first time to make gyoza.
...She mixed up the fillings and then filled the skins, and finally she cooked the gyoza.
We often have a mix of boiled and fried gyoza, but tonight we only had the fried version.

item.title: A Step in the Right Direction?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Actually as you may recall in a previous post, I’m more like Tim ‘The Tool Time’ Taylor from the show Home Improvement.
...The stairs I built 8 years ago, out the back of our dining room had been slowly disintegrating. Those stairs were made by accident as I was just playing around with scrap wood and before I knew it had built some stairs.
...The stairs came together over a couple of hours yesterday before dinnertime and were quickly covered up due to the threat of rain. ... Hopefully the memory will be stained on our brains over the years as we walk up and down these stairs.

item.title: Chim Chim Cher-ee
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I should also mention that the rods must pass through a small hole in a plastic bag, which is taped around the opening of the bottom of the chimney pipe. ... Once all the rods and brush have been removed, the plastic bag is carefully removed, the wood stove is moved into place, and the chimney pipe is once again connected. Finally the area is wiped down with a wet rag, as invariably some of the soot has seeped out through the pipe or my plastic bag.
...This led to little soot in the chimney pipe - we had less that 250 ml (or so) for 3 stories of pipe. I don’t know if this is good or bad compared to others, but we usually get a bit more soot than that so I’m happy we have less this year.

item.title: Strawberries
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I’m sure others have different suggestions such as coffee, BBQ or roses but for me, strawberries is definitely one option.
...One of my former student’s family invited us to come picking, as they have finished selling their strawberries for this season.
...In this way, we will enjoy the fruit now and over the next 6 months or so.
We really appreciate the kindness of our friends for inviting us and sharing their crops with us. Months from now, while having some jam on bread or pancakes we will smile and remember our friends.

item.title: Friday night fencing
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Our daughters started fencing a few years ago and thankfully they’ve kept at it. ... I constantly am reminded of Robin Hood, Peter Pan, pirates of all sorts, the Three Musketeers, and Gomez from the Addams Family when I see them fencing.
I’ve had the opportunity to try fencing with our daughters’ class and I loved it. It’s tiring to continue battling an opponent and it’s both exciting and scary to be attacking with your sword and being attacked by a sword. The fact that my daughters do this matter-of-factly makes me look at them with awe.

item.title: Just hanging around.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I’m actually precariously balanced on our longest ladder painting the railing on the second floor of our house. It’s a little tricky because the ladder, on the first floor has a limited area in which it can be put due to the wood stove (that’s the chimney pipe on my left side).
We’ve been doing some painting around our house lately, so if you smell the fumes or notice I have paint in my hair, on my ear or all over my hands, that’s the reason.
...I’m glad to be off of the ladder as it’s a bit shaky up there. I use a folding ladder that converts from the regular upside down ‘V’ to a fully extended straight ladder that allows me to touch the ceiling on the second floor.

item.title: A visit to Mugi.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
The scenery around the sea is completely different from what we have here in Naruto.
...Our visit included time with family, good food (sashimi to die for!), and beautiful nature.
We spent an afternoon at Uchizma playing in the sand and the water’s edge. We visited with our relatives (they run the minshuku or inn at the end of the beach - fantastic meals and hospitality if you should ever get a chance to visit!), enjoyed the sounds and views and relaxed.
...My guess is the morning was good (wetsuits were hanging out drying) and that they were waiting for the evening waves.

item.title: Some gardening.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
It sure doesn’t look like much from the photo, but this little garden produces a lot of little treats for us.
...Up and out of the way, we’ll be able to pick tomatoes as they hang down and we get to plant something else in our garden beds.
...Mixed in throughout all of that is a couple of other plants and more I’m sure that will come up due to mixing our kitchen compost into the soil.
At the far end of the yard there is mint, thyme, blueberries, two olive trees and a planter with tomato plants hanging over the wall.
...With some nice weather, a little luck, and even less insects, we should manage to get some food on our table this summer.

item.title: What is it with me and tools?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
At home, my help usually consisted of holding objects to stabilize them, leaving the real work to some one else (ANY one else). My father was the one who could make anything, fix anything, work with any tool, tackle any problem and actually enjoy, yes, enjoy working with his tools.
...I learned how to do a few repair jobs but with a family full of expertise and experience, I often did very little (more of that ‘holding’). Similarly, when I moved to Japan I bought the odd tool here and there and did some repair work here and there.
...My father-in-law realized what basic tools I need and provided me with the basics, for which I will forever be grateful.

item.title: Spring Cleaning?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I thought my wife was going to do some painting in a few areas. There are baseboards and door trimmings that we haven’t painted since we built the house (they were already painted with a white primer paint when we installed them.
...After a while, my other daughter joined in and we were painting in 3 rooms at once. Furniture was being moved, painting tape was being laid down, newspapers were put on the floor and the smell of paint permeated the house.
...Then again, you might notice the odd blob of paint that didn’t go where we wanted it to - on the wall, on the floor, on the tiles.

item.title: Cherry Blossoms
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded: Today we went to see the cherry blossoms.

item.title: Would my Baba be proud?
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
My family is Ukrainian and over my lifetime I’ve eaten a lot of borscht, but I have not made borscht that many times. Recently my brother sent some borscht concentrate that would save me the trouble of taking a drive to Tokushima to buy a can or two of beets for the soup.
...Watching and tasting my wife’s and my mother-in-law’s miso soups I came to realize that the base of the soup was so important. ... I noticed that starting the miso soup with some dashi and adding in various vegetables or other items and creating a flavourful broth helped to make a delicious miso soup.
...There’s the umami from the meat and vegetables that have cooked together, the sweet from the beets and some sugar added, the salty from salt, and the sour from vinegar or sour salt.

item.title: It's a good Friday.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
For my family, we had a pretty good day. We started off trying to see a circus that’s currently playing in Tokushima but when we arrived for the morning show we found lots of other families also in line and unfortunately we couldn’t see the show. Instead we went to a nearby shopping centre and did some shopping before coming home for lunch.
After lunch my daughters went shopping for some eggs, made up the dyes and decorated some eggs for Easter. ... I also love the fact that they cooked the eggs by themselves, did all the decorating alone AND did the final clean up by themselves.

item.title: A visit to Mugi.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
When I came to Japan I believed that seafood in Japan would be plentiful and cheap. ... It’s hard to think that way for me because this country has access to the seas from nearly any place in the country. Much different from when I lived in Canada and would have to drive for days before I came to the oceans.
...Fish that I find for sale at fish markets or supermarkets that, before I had the Mugi experience, I would have gladly eaten as sashimi, are now seen as less than perfect and are eaten differently.
...While in Mugi we ate a variety of fresh fish and other foods as well, all of them being very delicious.

item.title: Chocolate Marshmallow Pie
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
We still have a lot of chocolate leftover that was bought to use for Valentine’s baking but was never used. ... The marshmallows are not old, but I haven’t seen the bag for a week or two and finding it today was a surprise.
I did a search for recipes on the internet but none of them fit exactly with what I had in mind, so today’s pie was an experiment.
...I’m sorry the picture above does not do the pie justice, but to tell you the truth I’d rather spend my time eating and enjoying the food with my family than playing around with the food and a camera. From the picture I’m sure you can tell it’s a chocolate pie and tastes fantastic.

item.title: Today's cooking lesson.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
On top of the bananas is whipped cream, with a coffee syrup folded in.
...The students were served this pie at last month’s cooking lesson, but there wasn’t time to teach how to make it at that time. ... The pie isn’t that hard to make, but each step takes a bit of time. Mostly, it is just the time between steps that makes this pie take a long time to come together.
...A one-dish wonder that is pretty easy to prepare and yet has a deep, rich taste to it.

item.title: William Tell
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I believe that everyone in the household was of legal drinking age by this time, and so helping one family member to make a wine or beer was not disagreeable in the least.
...Again, boys being boys we decided to put in some sort of punishment for the loser, and idea of having the loser drink some of that awful banana beer was born.
...A beer usually brews up to about 5-7% alcohol, but it doesn’t go much higher because the strain of yeast used for beer dies out if the alcohol is too high. ... So it seems that while we had put in beer yeast to make the banana beer, some champagne yeast had also been added as a back-up.
...But, and this is serendipity, the bananas converted into a lot of sugars for the yeasts to work on, and once the beer yeast had died out, the champagne yeast kept going.

item.title: Getting ready for White Day
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I know they don’t look like much, but a lot of time and effort went into their making and I think they taste pretty good.
...Valentine’s Day on February 14th is often celebrated in Japan with females giving chocolates or sweets to males. I think this can be a lot of pressure on females thinking they should give something to males for this celebration. ... One month later, there are some items for sale to celebrate White Day, but the amount is very small in comparison with Valentine’s Day.
I have been fortunate over the years to receive chocolates and sweets from some students on Valentine’s Day, and I do my best to show my appreciation one month later on White Day.

item.title: I'm a Diubach!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
Well, from what I’ve been told, it’s Gaelic for people of Jura, an area of Scotland.
...I detect nuances of grapes leading me to wonder if the Whisky matures in Sherry casks for part of its life.
...Jura Whisky is very generous to its patrons because by becoming a Diubach (free), I may now receive a free dram of their Whisky each month, for life! ... There’s just the little matter of airfare and accommodations that I have to take care of, and then I’m there.
Perhaps, if I build a summer home on my property in Scotland (a wee little place) I’ll solve the accommodation problem and just have to deal with the airfare.

item.title: Pita, pita, pumpkin eater.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Oh, I’m making some little meatballs that will be fried then cooked in a braising liquid, and some chickpea hummus, and some other vegetables to go inside, but the only food I can be sure of that everyone will eat will be the pitas.
The dough is easy enough to make and is just a basic bread dough. The cooking is where this bread changes from any other bread into pitas. I make little balls of dough, then roll them out into small circles before baking them in a hot oven. They all puffed up nicely and will be good to eat with anything.

item.title: Whatcha eatin'? Naan of your business!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
I finished making today’s curry earlier in the day and therefore had lots of time to make some naan. ... My kids usually want naan to go along with the curry, but because I can make curry quickly I often make it late in the day and therefore don’t have the time to do the naan.
...I’ve collected a number of them and they’ve all generally been OK, but I thought I’d keep looking. The picture of the naan bread I found looked pretty close to what I was after, so I used that recipe.
...My kids will eat the lion’s share of them, though and I foresee no complaints coming from them.

item.title: Banana Chocolate Pie
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
This, my friends is a great pie!
The crust has a bit more salt added to it compared with a regular fruit pie crust.
...Next is a banana-caramel layer which is soft, sweet and banana-y.
After that, bananas are sliced over the caramel layer.
Then, cream is whipped and then a coffee syrup is mixed in.

item.title: Today's cooking class.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
Today’s menu wasn’t exactly diet fare, but considering the fact that we rarely eat like this, I have no qualms about today’s lunch.
...It was finished under our oven’s grill which doesn’t heat evenly, but it was browned all over (not burned) and was nice and bubbly.
...This dish has a beautiful smell from the herbs and mustard, and by browning the chicken first the dish picks up a light golden colour and extra flavours. My kids generally do not eat mustard but that did not stop them from devouring this dish when I made it.
...When I’m at home for lunch I never eat this way, but when I’ve gone out to a restaurant I’ve had similar lunches.

item.title: Look who's back.
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I don’t know why and I don’t know how, but he’s back.
Not a lot of talking took place between the two of us. ... You can see the results of our efforts in the background.
I think it’ll be better if we just put the past behind us and deal with things in the present.
So, now both blue boy and orange boy are back to work with nary a complaint between them.

item.title: Bad Boys
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.content:encoded:
I picked it up cheap, and though not too powerful, it is electric and can be used for cutting smaller pieces of wood when I don’t want or need to use the bigger chainsaw.
...I picked up a huge pile of wood over the last week and then we had 4 days of rain so I couldn’t cut it into more manageable pieces.
...Smoke coming from the wood being cut, and burn marks on the wood are never good signs when using a gas chainsaw, at least from my limited experience and knowledge.
...After putting on the new chain and cleaning the chainsaw (orange boy) - something I hadn’t done in a while - I got ready to do some cutting.
...I decided to check on blue boy, but no, it still wouldn’t start. 30 minutes later, after taking it completely apart and plugging it in, it was spinning away, laughing at me.

item.title: Holy Smoke!
item.dc:creator: Canada Club English School
item.dc:subject: ブログ（英語）
item.content:encoded:
And this liquid smoke, もくさくえき/mokusaku eki in Japanese, which is locally produced is a favourite of mine.
...In the kitchen, it’s used for getting rid of smells from food waste waiting to be put into our compost pile outside. I also like to use it at times when I’m cooking, as an ingredient in the recipe.
...A squirt of this inside a stinky or soon to be stinky shoe makes your feet smell like a sausage or smokey campfire.
...I’ve been using this product for a few years now, and every year I receive a New Year’s postcard from the owner.
